400+ Arch Linux AUR Packages Hijacked to Install Rust Credential Stealer

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 18 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Attackers took over more than 400 packages in the Arch User Repository (AUR) this week and rewrote their build scripts to install a credential stealer on any machine that built them. The malware is a Rust binary built to harvest developer secrets. When it lands with root, it can also load an eBPF rootkit to hide itself. The AUR is Arch Linux's community package collection, and it is separate

Atomic Arch AUR build invokes 'npm install atomic-lockfile' or 'bun install js-digest' AIInstallation High
Detects the build-time payload trigger: makepkg / fakeroot / bash spawning npm or bun with the malicious package names embedded in hijacked PKGBUILD or .install scripts. This is the single highest-fidelity choke point — the package names are unique to this campaign. Rationale: Pivots on the two malicious npm package names ('atomic-lockfile', 'js-digest') called out in the article and the kill-chain reconstruction's Phase 3 detection hint, narrowed by AUR-build parents (makepkg / fakeroot / shell). These strings are unique to the Atomic Arch campaign — no legitimate AUR build pulls these packages. Cross-checked against the article's citations of Sonatype's Atomic Arch write-up and the Arch aur-general mailing-list thread referencing alvr and premake-git.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.004 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher voluntarily reproducing the IOC in a lab (legitimate but matches)
  • Internal post-incident validation where the package was reinstalled to study behaviour
  • Honeypot / canary host deliberately pulling the package
  • Mirror of the malicious package in a private offline repo for IR purposes
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dry-run", "--help") or AccountName in~ ("ir-sandbox", "malware-lab"))
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Confirm the host actually built the AUR package — pull the full PKGBUILD/.install diff from /var/cache/pacman/ and the user's makepkg working dir. Identify which AUR package was being built. 2. CONTAIN: Isolate the host from the network immediately — treat as credential-compromised. Snapshot /sys/fs/bpf/, ~/.config/systemd/user/, /etc/systemd/system/, and /var/lib/ before reboot to preserve rootkit artefacts. 3. HUNT: Across the fleet, look for any other host that ran 'npm install atomic-lockfile' or 'bun install js-digest' in the last 30 days; rotate every credential the stealer touches (browsers, SSH, GitHub/npm tokens, Vault, Docker, cloud keys). If build ran as root, reimage — package removal is insufficient per article's eBPF-rootkit guidance.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm", "bun")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("atomic-lockfile", "js-digest")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("makepkg", "fakeroot", "bash", "sh", "zsh", "dash")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKGBUILD", ".install", "makepkg")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd  = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentFolder = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "/npm" or TargetProcessName endswith "/bun"
   or TargetProcessName in~ ("npm", "bun")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKGBUILD", ".install", "makepkg")
   or ActingProcessName has_any ("makepkg", "fakeroot", "bash", "sh", "zsh")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("atomic-lockfile", "js-digest")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          Parent = ActingProcessName, ParentCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          Child = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Atomic Arch 'deps' ELF execution by hash or src/hooks/deps path AIInstallation Medium
Catches the bundled Rust credential stealer the moment it executes — either by its published SHA-256 6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b or by the canonical npm-preinstall payload path 'src/hooks/deps'. Hash hit is alert-grade; path hit is hunting-grade because npm preinstall hooks legitimately exist in /src/hooks/. Rationale: Uses the article's published payload SHA-256 6144d433…3c98b and MD5 42b59fdb…f40, plus the kill-chain Phase 3 detection hint 'src/hooks/deps'. Hash match alone is a slam-dunk; the path + npm-parent fallback catches recompiled variants where the hash changes. Cross-checked against the ioctl.fail analysis referenced in the article.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate npm package that happens to ship a binary at src/hooks/deps (path-only branch)
  • Malware analyst running the sample in a sandbox VM
  • Threat-intel team reproducing the IOC for detection validation
  • Backup/archive of the AUR package preserved for forensic study
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Confirm the hash match against the original article-published SHA-256 (no transposition errors). Pull the parent process tree — npm/bun/node parent confirms the Atomic Arch chain; any other parent suggests a copy/relocation by an operator. 2. CONTAIN: Network-isolate the host; the article warns rootkit may be active. Capture memory and /sys/fs/bpf/ contents before any reboot. Block the SHA-256 at the EDR. 3. HUNT: Search 90 days of telemetry for the same hash anywhere in the fleet. Pivot to UC #1 (npm install atomic-lockfile / bun install js-digest) on the same host to identify which AUR package was the carrier. Treat all developer credentials touched in last 30 days as compromised — rotate per article guidance.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 == "6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b"
   or MD5 == "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"
   or FolderPath has "/src/hooks/deps"
   or (FileName =~ "deps" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm", "node", "bun"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Cmd = ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 =~ "6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b"
   or MD5 =~ "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"
   or TargetProcessName has "/src/hooks/deps"
   or (TargetProcessName endswith "/deps" and ActingProcessName has_any ("npm", "node", "bun"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          Child = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine,
          Parent = ActingProcessName, ParentCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, MD5

Atomic Arch systemd persistence — Restart=always unit dropped outside package manager AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the stealer's persistence mechanism: a new .service file under /etc/systemd/system/ (root mode) or ~/.config/systemd/user/ (user mode), written by a process that isn't pacman / dpkg / systemctl, followed shortly by an ELF drop under /var/lib/. Catches both privileged and unprivileged persistence variants from the article. Rationale: Targets the article's Phase 4 persistence behaviour verbatim: 'systemd service with Restart=always … with root it copies itself under /var/lib/ and writes a unit under /etc/systemd/system/; as a normal user it uses … ~/.config/systemd/user/'. Excludes known package-manager / systemctl writers to suppress legitimate installs. The DeviceFileEvents join on payload drops under /var/lib/ within ±5m matches the article's two-step persistence (binary + unit).
ATT&CKT1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible / Puppet / Salt / Chef installing custom systemd units via a Python or Ruby runtime
  • Developer manually creating a user-mode systemd unit for a personal service
  • Third-party installer script (e.g. Docker / NVIDIA driver installer) writing units outside pacman
  • Container engine (containerd / podman quadlet generators) writing transient units
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible-playbook", "salt-minion", "puppet", "chef-client", "cloud-init")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: cat the .service file — read ExecStart= and check whether the binary is under /var/lib/, ~/.local/, or any unusual path. Look for 'Restart=always' as the article called out. 2. CONTAIN: systemctl disable + stop the unit, but DO NOT delete the binary yet — capture for IR. If the unit ran as root, treat host as rootkit-capable and reimage per article guidance. 3. HUNT: Across the fleet, list all systemd units written in the past 30 days where the writer wasn't a package manager. Cross-reference against UC #1 (npm install atomic-lockfile) to find the build event that planted it.
let suspicious_units = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
    | where FolderPath matches regex @"^/etc/systemd/system/[^/]+\.service$"
         or FolderPath matches regex @"\.config/systemd/user/[^/]+\.service$"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("pacman", "makepkg", "systemctl", "systemd", "apt", "apt-get", "dpkg", "yay", "paru", "snapd", "dnf", "rpm");
let payload_drops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
    | where FolderPath startswith "/var/lib/" or FolderPath has "/.config/"
    | where FileSize between (50000 .. 50000000)
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DropPath = FolderPath, DropProc = InitiatingProcessFileName, DropSHA = SHA256;
suspicious_units
| join kind=inner payload_drops on DeviceId
| where DropTime between (Timestamp - 5m .. Timestamp + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, UnitPath = FolderPath,
          UnitWrittenBy = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          UnitWriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          DropPath, DropProc, DropSHA
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"^/etc/systemd/system/[^/]+\.service$"
     or TargetFilePath matches regex @"\.config/systemd/user/[^/]+\.service$"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("pacman", "makepkg", "systemctl", "systemd", "apt", "apt-get", "dpkg", "yay", "paru", "snapd", "dnf", "rpm")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          UnitPath = TargetFilePath,
          WrittenBy = ActingProcessName,
          WriterCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256 = TargetFileSHA256

Atomic Arch eBPF rootkit — pinned BPF map named hidden_pids / hidden_names / hidden_inodes AIInstallation High
Targets the very specific eBPF rootkit fingerprint the article identifies: pinned BPF maps named hidden_pids, hidden_names, hidden_inodes appearing under /sys/fs/bpf/. These names are unique to this campaign; any file create under /sys/fs/bpf/hidden_* is a virtual smoking gun. Rationale: Verbatim string match on the article-quoted BPF map names ('pinned BPF maps named hidden_pids, hidden_names, and hidden_inodes'). These are unique enough that any hit is essentially a confirmed compromise — there's no benign reason for a Linux host to expose maps with those names under /sys/fs/bpf/. This is also the article's explicit IR check: 'Inspect /sys/fs/bpf/ for the maps hidden_pids, hidden_names, and hidden_inodes.'
ATT&CKT1014 T1562.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • None expected on real production hosts — these specific map names are campaign-unique
  • Red team / purple team running an Atomic Arch emulation exercise
  • Detection engineer testing this very rule in a controlled VM
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: ssh in (or use a side-channel like serial console — stealer hides processes from standard tools), run `bpftool map list` and `bpftool prog list` to enumerate loaded BPF programs. Run `ls -la /sys/fs/bpf/hidden_*`. 2. CONTAIN: This is a rootkit-confirmed host. Per article: 'There is no way to trust the system otherwise.' Capture forensic image, then reimage from trusted media. Rotate every credential the host had access to. 3. HUNT: Across the fleet, check /sys/fs/bpf/ on every Linux dev/build host. Pivot to UC #1 / #2 to identify which AUR package was the carrier. Treat all hosts that ran the same package as rootkit-suspect even if /sys/fs/bpf/ is currently clean (article notes rootkit only loads when root + capability available).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where FileName in~ ("hidden_pids", "hidden_names", "hidden_inodes")
   or FolderPath has_any ("/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_pids", "/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_names", "/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_inodes")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType,
          FolderPath, FileName,
          WrittenBy = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterFolder = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("hidden_pids", "hidden_names", "hidden_inodes")
   or TargetFilePath has_any ("/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_pids", "/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_names", "/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_inodes")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          WrittenBy = ActingProcessName,
          WriterCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetFileSHA256

detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_pids'
      - '/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_names'
      - '/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_inodes'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - None expected — these map names are unique to this campaign
level: critical
source:linux.auditd @file.path:(*"/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_pids"* OR *"/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_names"* OR *"/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_inodes"*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten #event_platform=Lin
| TargetFileName=/\/sys\/fs\/bpf\/hidden_(pids|names|inodes)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_pids*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_names*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_inodes*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name("Filesystem")`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_pids*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_names*" OR Filesystem.file_path="/sys/fs/bpf/hidden_inodes*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name("Filesystem")`
Atomic Arch credential file fan-out — non-browser process reads browser / SSH / Vault secrets after AUR build AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the article's Phase 6 credential harvest: a process (typically the deps ELF) reading multiple developer-credential file types — browser cookies, SSH keys, npm/Vault tokens, Docker creds — within minutes of an AUR build. The fan-out across file categories is the signal; single-file reads are noise. Rationale: Maps directly to the article's Phase 6 detection hint ('non-browser processes reading ~/.config/google-chrome/, ~/.mozilla, Slack/Discord/Teams Electron storage, ~/.ssh/, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.npmrc, and ~/.vault-token within seconds of an AUR build'). The DistinctTargets >= 3 threshold isolates true credential fan-out (the stealer touches all categories) from legitimate single-file reads (e.g. ssh reading id_ed25519). Allowlists the legitimate owner processes per category.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1552.001 T1552.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup agents (restic, borg, rclone) reading the user's home directory wholesale
  • Antivirus / EDR scanning passes touching multiple credential files in quick succession
  • Developer-tooling like 1Password CLI / pass / KeePassXC reading multiple credential stores
  • Cloud-sync clients (Dropbox / Google Drive) indexing the user's home directory
  • grep / find / ripgrep / fd run by a sysadmin or developer over their home directory
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("restic", "borg", "rclone", "rsync", "backup-agent", "clamscan", "freshclam", "1password-cli", "pass", "keepassxc", "dropbox", "google-drive-ocamlfuse", "grep", "rg", "fd", "find", "locate", "updatedb")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Identify the reading process — get full path, SHA-256, and parent chain. If parent is npm/bun/node and the binary path includes /src/hooks/ or /var/lib/ → cross-confirm with UC #1/#2. 2. CONTAIN: Network-isolate the host. Immediately rotate every credential touched: browser sessions (force-revoke), SSH keys (regenerate + push new pubkeys, revoke old in authorized_keys org-wide), GitHub/npm PATs (revoke at provider), Vault tokens (revoke at Vault), Docker/Podman registry creds, Slack/Discord/Teams sessions (sign-out-all). 3. HUNT: Pull DeviceNetworkEvents for the same host — look for HTTP POSTs to temp.sh (UC #7) or Tor loopback (UC #6) to confirm exfil happened. Pivot to UC #4 to check for rootkit; if present, reimage.
let CredTargets = dynamic([
  "/.config/google-chrome/", "/.config/chromium/", "/.config/BraveSoftware/",
  "/.config/microsoft-edge/", "/.mozilla/firefox/", "/.ssh/id_",
  "/.ssh/known_hosts", "/.npmrc", "/.vault-token", "/.docker/config.json",
  "/.config/Slack/", "/.config/discord/", "/.config/Microsoft/Microsoft Teams/",
  "/.bash_history", "/.zsh_history", "/.config/podman/"
]);
let AllowedReaders = dynamic([
  "chrome", "chromium", "firefox", "firefox-bin", "brave", "msedge",
  "slack", "discord", "teams", "ssh", "sshd", "git", "git-credential",
  "npm", "node", "docker", "dockerd", "podman", "vault", "gpg", "gnome-keyring",
  "bash", "zsh", "fish"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened", "FileAccessed")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredTargets)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (AllowedReaders)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(FolderPath),
            TouchedSample = make_set(FolderPath, 25),
            FirstAccess = min(Timestamp), LastAccess = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
               InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
| order by DistinctTargets desc
let CredTargets = dynamic([
  "/.config/google-chrome/", "/.config/chromium/", "/.config/BraveSoftware/",
  "/.config/microsoft-edge/", "/.mozilla/firefox/", "/.ssh/id_",
  "/.ssh/known_hosts", "/.npmrc", "/.vault-token", "/.docker/config.json",
  "/.config/Slack/", "/.config/discord/", "/.config/Microsoft/Microsoft Teams/",
  "/.bash_history", "/.zsh_history", "/.config/podman/"
]);
let AllowedReaders = dynamic([
  "chrome", "chromium", "firefox", "firefox-bin", "brave", "msedge",
  "slack", "discord", "teams", "ssh", "sshd", "git", "git-credential",
  "npm", "node", "docker", "dockerd", "podman", "vault", "gpg", "gnome-keyring",
  "bash", "zsh", "fish"
]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed", "FileOpened", "FileRead")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredTargets)
| extend ActorBase = tostring(split(ActingProcessName, "/")[-1])
| where ActorBase !in~ (AllowedReaders)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Targets = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
            FirstAccess = min(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActorBase, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(SYSCALL OR PATH) (@file.path:(*"/.config/google-chrome/Cookies"* OR *"/.config/chromium/Cookies"* OR *"/.config/BraveSoftware/"*"/Cookies"* OR *"/.mozilla/firefox/"*"/cookies.sqlite"* OR *"/.ssh/id_"* OR *"/.npmrc"* OR *"/.vault-token"* OR *"/.docker/config.json"* OR *"/.config/Slack/"* OR *"/.config/discord/"* OR *"/.config/Microsoft/Microsoft Teams/"*)) -@process.name:(chrome OR chromium OR firefox OR brave OR msedge OR slack OR discord OR teams OR ssh OR git OR npm OR node OR docker OR podman OR vault OR gpg OR bash OR zsh)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo #event_platform=Lin
| TargetFileName=/(\/\.config\/(google-chrome|chromium|BraveSoftware|microsoft-edge|Slack|discord|Microsoft\/Microsoft\sTeams)\/|\/\.mozilla\/firefox\/|\/\.ssh\/(id_|known_hosts)|\/\.npmrc$|\/\.vault-token$|\/\.docker\/config\.json$|\/\.config\/podman\/|\/\.bash_history$|\/\.zsh_history$)/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(chrome|chromium|firefox|firefox-bin|brave|msedge|slack|discord|teams|ssh|sshd|git|git-credential|npm|node|docker|dockerd|podman|vault|gpg|gnome-keyring|bash|zsh|fish)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, SHA256HashData], function={ count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctTargets) | count(as=TotalReads) })
| DistinctTargets >= 3
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_path) as touched_files dc(Filesystem.file_name) as distinct_files min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="read" (Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/google-chrome/*Cookies*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/chromium/*Cookies*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/BraveSoftware/*Cookies*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/microsoft-edge/*Cookies*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.mozilla/firefox/*/cookies.sqlite" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/known_hosts" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.vault-token" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/Slack/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/discord/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/Microsoft/Microsoft Teams/*") (Filesystem.process_name!="chrome" Filesystem.process_name!="firefox" Filesystem.process_name!="brave" Filesystem.process_name!="msedge" Filesystem.process_name!="slack" Filesystem.process_name!="discord" Filesystem.process_name!="teams" Filesystem.process_name!="ssh" Filesystem.process_name!="git" Filesystem.process_name!="npm" Filesystem.process_name!="docker" Filesystem.process_name!="vault") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name("Filesystem")` | where distinct_files >= 3
Atomic Arch Tor loopback C2 — process connects to 127.0.0.1:9050/9150 right after AUR build AICommand & Control Medium
Detects the article's Phase 7 C2 channel: the stealer reaches its Tor onion via a local loopback proxy (Tor default 9050, Tor Browser 9150). Hunts processes that aren't a Tor client or Tor Browser connecting to those loopback ports — most useful when correlated with a recent AUR build on the same host. Rationale: Hits the article's Phase 7 detection hint verbatim ('Alert on unexpected processes binding/connecting to 127.0.0.1:9050/9150') and the C2-via-Tor-loopback IOC. The exclusion list covers Tor Browser (which legitimately uses these ports) — anything else hitting them is suspect. Confidence is Medium not High because some privacy-conscious developers run custom Tor clients, but a fleet-baseline filter or join with UC #1 within 1h elevates to High.
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer with privacy tools (Tails, Whonix workstation) connecting custom apps through local Tor
  • Researcher running OnionShare or Ricochet (legitimately uses local Tor)
  • BitTorrent / IRC client configured to route over Tor SOCKS
  • Curl / wget invoked manually via --socks5 127.0.0.1:9050 for legitimate research
  • Tor service health-check script polling 9051 (control port)
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("privacy-research", "redteam") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has_any ("/tails/", "/whonix/")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Identify the connecting process — get binary path + SHA-256. If path is under /var/lib/, ~/.local/share/, or matches the deps ELF (UC #2), confidence rises to confirmed. Also check whether the host has Tor installed at all — if not, the stealer is bundling its own Tor client. 2. CONTAIN: Network-isolate; block 127.0.0.1:9050 outbound at endpoint firewall (or kill the local tor process). Capture all network state before reboot. 3. HUNT: Across the fleet, pivot on the same SHA-256 plus 127.0.0.1:9050 to spot lateral spread. Pull DNS / proxy logs for resolution of any .onion or for outbound connections to Tor guard relay IPs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIPType in ("Loopback", "Private")
| where RemoteIP in ("127.0.0.1", "::1")
| where RemotePort in (9050, 9051, 9150)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("tor", "firefox", "firefox-bin", "torbrowser", "tor-browser", "nyx", "arm", "obfs4proxy")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has "tor-browser"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatorFolder = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatorSHA = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("127.0.0.1", "::1")
| where DstPortNumber in (9050, 9051, 9150)
| extend Initiator = tostring(split(SrcUsername, "/")[-1])
| where Initiator !in~ ("tor", "firefox", "firefox-bin", "torbrowser", "tor-browser", "nyx", "arm", "obfs4proxy")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes
title: Non-Tor process connects to local Tor SOCKS proxy port
id: 8b1f3a72-4c5e-4d92-9b1a-7f2e3c4d5b06
status: experimental
description: Detects a process connecting to 127.0.0.1:9050 / 9051 / 9150 that isn't a known Tor client or Tor Browser instance. Matches the Atomic Arch stealer's Tor-loopback C2 channel.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/400-arch-linux-aur-packages-hijacked-to.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1090.003

logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationIp:
      - '127.0.0.1'
      - '::1'
    DestinationPort:
      - 9050
      - 9051
      - 9150
  filter_tor:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/tor'
      - '/firefox'
      - '/firefox-bin'
      - '/torbrowser'
      - '/tor-browser'
      - '/obfs4proxy'
  filter_tb_folder:
    Image|contains: 'tor-browser'
  condition: selection and not (filter_tor or filter_tb_folder)
level: medium
source:linux.auditd (@network.destination.ip:127.0.0.1 OR @network.destination.ip:::1) @network.destination.port:(9050 OR 9051 OR 9150) -@process.name:(tor OR firefox OR firefox-bin OR torbrowser OR tor-browser OR obfs4proxy OR nyx OR arm) -@process.executable.path:*tor-browser*
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 #event_platform=Lin
| RemoteAddressIP4="127.0.0.1"
| RemotePort=9050 OR RemotePort=9051 OR RemotePort=9150
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(tor|firefox|firefox-bin|torbrowser|tor-browser|obfs4proxy|nyx|arm)$/i
| NOT regex("tor-browser", field=ContextImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="127.0.0.1" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="::1") (All_Traffic.dest_port=9050 OR All_Traffic.dest_port=9150 OR All_Traffic.dest_port=9051) (All_Traffic.process_name!="tor" All_Traffic.process_name!="firefox" All_Traffic.process_name!="torbrowser*" All_Traffic.process_name!="tor-browser*" All_Traffic.process_name!="nyx" All_Traffic.process_name!="arm") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process_path All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name("All_Traffic")`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="127.0.0.1" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="::1") (All_Traffic.dest_port=9050 OR All_Traffic.dest_port=9150 OR All_Traffic.dest_port=9051) (All_Traffic.process_name!="tor" All_Traffic.process_name!="firefox" All_Traffic.process_name!="torbrowser*" All_Traffic.process_name!="tor-browser*" All_Traffic.process_name!="nyx" All_Traffic.process_name!="arm") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process_path All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name("All_Traffic")`
Atomic Arch exfil — HTTP upload to temp.sh from a developer / build host AIActions on Objectives Medium
Catches the article's Phase 8 exfiltration: stolen credential bundles POSTed over HTTP to temp.sh. Detects either the DNS lookup for temp.sh or an outbound HTTP connection to its IPs from a process that isn't a known user-facing browser / curl invocation. Rationale: Pivots on the article-named exfil domain temp.sh (Phase 8: 'Stolen files go out over HTTP to temp.sh') and the kill-chain detection hint ('Alert on HTTP POST/PUT uploads to temp.sh … originating from developer workstations or build agents, especially correlated with prior makepkg activity'). Excludes browsers because temp.sh is a legitimate paste/upload service that humans do use — the signal is the non-browser caller, especially when paired with UC #1 firing on the same host within 1h.
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually using temp.sh to share a build log or a screenshot via curl
  • CI script uploading test artefacts to temp.sh
  • Sysadmin using temp.sh to share a diagnostic over Slack
  • Penetration tester legitimately using temp.sh as a drop site during an engagement
  • Browser extensions invoking native messaging helpers that fetch via curl/wget
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("build-artifact", "ci-debug", "--share-log") and AccountName !in~ ("ci-runner", "jenkins", "gitlab-runner")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Identify uploading process — binary path + SHA-256. Check upload size; the article describes credential bundles, so 100KB-10MB POSTs are likely. Try to capture the URL path (the temp.sh-assigned slug) for IR reference. 2. CONTAIN: Block temp.sh at the proxy / DNS sinkhole for the affected segment. Network-isolate the host. Capture any local copies of the staged exfil bundle (often in /tmp/ or under the malware's working dir) before reboot. 3. HUNT: Across the fleet, search 90 days for any host that resolved or connected to temp.sh. Cross-correlate with UC #1/#2 firings to scope the blast radius. Assume any credential touched by UC #5 on those hosts is now in attacker hands and rotate accordingly.
let DnsHits = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
    | where AdditionalFields has "temp.sh"
    | project DnsTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DnsAdditional = AdditionalFields;
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has "temp.sh" or RemoteUrl endswith "temp.sh"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("firefox", "firefox-bin", "chrome", "chromium", "brave", "msedge", "safari")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName,
              Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatorFolder = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              InitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatorSHA = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
              RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort;
NetHits
| union (DnsHits | extend NoteOnly = "DNS only — no HTTP yet")
| order by Timestamp desc
let DnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where DnsQuery has "temp.sh" or DnsQuery endswith "temp.sh"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery;
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Url has "temp.sh" or HttpHostName endswith "temp.sh"
    | extend ActorBase = tostring(split(SrcUsername, "/")[-1])
    | where ActorBase !in~ ("firefox", "firefox-bin", "chrome", "chromium", "brave", "msedge", "safari")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestBodyBytes;
WebHits
| union DnsHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HTTP / DNS to temp.sh from non-browser process (Atomic Arch exfil)
id: 9c2e5b81-6f3d-4a8c-92f4-1d3e6b7c8a05
status: experimental
description: Detects an outbound connection or DNS lookup to temp.sh originating from a process that isn't a known web browser. Matches the Atomic Arch credential-stealer exfil channel.
references:

logsource:
  category: dns
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith: 'temp.sh'
  filter_browser:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/firefox'
      - '/firefox-bin'
      - '/chrome'
      - '/chromium'
      - '/brave'
      - '/msedge'
      - '/safari'
  condition: selection and not filter_browser
level: high
source:linux.auditd (@dns.question.name:*temp.sh OR @network.destination.domain:*temp.sh OR @http.url:*temp.sh*) -@process.name:(firefox OR firefox-bin OR chrome OR chromium OR brave OR msedge OR safari)
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4) #event_platform=Lin
| (DomainName=/(^|\.)temp\.sh$/i OR ContextImageFileName!="")
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(firefox|firefox-bin|chrome|chromium|brave|msedge|safari)$/i
| regex("temp\\.sh", field=DomainName) OR regex("temp\\.sh", field=HttpHost)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as ports min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.url="*temp.sh*" OR All_Traffic.dest="temp.sh" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.temp.sh") (All_Traffic.process_name!="firefox" All_Traffic.process_name!="chrome" All_Traffic.process_name!="chromium" All_Traffic.process_name!="brave" All_Traffic.process_name!="msedge" All_Traffic.process_name!="safari") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.process_path All_Traffic.url | `drop_dm_object_name("All_Traffic")`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

DeviceNetworkEvents

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["temp.sh", "olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion"]);
ImNetworkSession

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |

author: Clankerusecase

detection:

APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40") or SHA1 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40") or MD5 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40") or SHA1 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40") or MD5 in~ ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b", "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-21509", "CVE-2023-50224")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-21509", "CVE-2023-50224")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-21509", "CVE-2023-50224")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-21509", "CVE-2023-50224")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("freefoodaid.com", "wellnesscaremed.com", "wellnessmedcare.org", "longsauce.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["freefoodaid.com", "wellnesscaremed.com", "wellnessmedcare.org", "longsauce.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b2ba51b4491da8604ff9410d6e004971e3cd9a321390d0258e294ac42010b546", "1ed863a32372160b3a25549aad25d48d5352d9b4f58d4339408c4eea69807f50", "5a17cfaea0cc3a82242fdd11b53140c0b56256d769b07c33757d61e0a0a6ec02", "fd3f13db41cd5b442fa26ba8bc0e9703ed243b3516374e3ef89be71cbf07436b", "c91183175ce77360006f964841eb4048cf37cb82103f2573e262927be4c7607f", "a944a09783023a2c6c62d3601cbd5392a03d808a6a51728e07a3270861c2a8ee", "bb23545380fde9f48ad070f88fe0afd695da5fcae8c5274814858c5a681d8c4e", "0bb0d54033767f081cae775e3cf9ede7ae6bea75f35fbfb748ccba9325e28e5e", "a876f648991711e44a8dcf888a271880c6c930e5138f284cd6ca6128eca56ba1", "2822c72a59b58c00fc088aa551cdeeb92ca10fd23e23745610ff207f53118db9", "9f4672c1374034ac4556264f0d4bf96ee242c0b5a9edaa4715b5e61fe8d55cc8", "3f476d316efe2514efd70c975d0c87e12357db9fca54a25834d60b28192c6a69"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Budibase CVE-2026-48150: POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign granting global builder/admin AIExploitation High
Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-48150 where a workspace-scoped builder calls the public API roles-assign endpoint with builder:true or admin:true in the request body to escalate themselves or others to tenant-wide global admin. Hunts the specific URL path, method, and x-budibase-app-id / x-budibase-api-key header pair the PoC uses. Rationale: Targets the exact vulnerable URL path /api/public/v1/roles/assign and POST method from the controller at packages/server/src/api/controllers/public/roles.ts:13-17 cited in the advisory. POST 200/201 on this endpoint is the unambiguous exploitation signal — the endpoint only exists for role assignment, so any successful authenticated POST is detection-worthy and should be cross-referenced with the actor's prior privilege scope. Corroborated against the GHSA advisory and Budibase commit history. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6xp4-cf37-ppjh • https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1068 T1078.004 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate global-admin onboarding new builders via the public API after Enterprise license enables EXPANDED_PUBLIC_API
  • Terraform / IaC scripts provisioning Budibase users in CI pipelines
  • SCIM connector calls reconciling role state from an upstream identity provider
  • Budibase admin UI itself proxying to the public API during user-management workflows
  • Penetration testing / vulnerability scanning explicitly targeting GHSA-6xp4-cf37-ppjh
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("terraform", "budibase-scim", "budibase-cli") and cIP !in (dynamic(["<known-iac-egress-ip>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the source IP, x-budibase-api-key user identity (resolve via GET /api/global/users), and request body. Confirm the caller does NOT already hold builder.global=true or admin.global=true — that is the escalation signal. 2) Contain: in Budibase admin console, revoke the API key for the caller, reset builder.global / admin.global for any userIds named in the request body, restore prior workspace-scoped builder.apps for stripped targets, and upgrade @budibase/server to >= 3.39.0. 3) Hunt: look back 30 days for any POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign by non-global-admin identities, GET /api/global/self/api_key calls from the same identities (key minting), and any AuditLog entries showing builder.global or admin.global flipping on accounts that subsequently logged in. Audit datasource credentials, automations and SCIM/OIDC configs touched by escalated accounts.
// Budibase CVE-2026-48150 exploitation — POST to public roles/assign endpoint succeeding

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// Budibase CVE-2026-48150 exploitation — POST to /api/public/v1/roles/assign
// W3CIISLog branch (on-prem / IIS-fronted Budibase). Pair with the AppServiceHTTPLogs branch if Budibase runs on Azure App Service.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where csUriStem has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
| where scStatus in (200, 201)
| where csUserName != ""  // authenticated call
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, sPort
| union (
    AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
    | where CsUriStem has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
    | where ScStatus in (200, 201)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = CsHost, sSiteName = CsHost, cIP = CIp, csUserName = CsUsername, csUserAgent = UserAgent, csMethod = CsMethod, csUriStem = CsUriStem, csUriQuery = CsUriQuery, scStatus = ScStatus, sPort = toint(0)
)

    | where toint(EventOutcome) in (200, 201) or DeviceAction in~ ("allow", "allowed")

)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Budibase CVE-2026-48150: API key mint immediately followed by public roles/assign call (escalation chain) AIExploitation Medium
Correlates the two-step exploit sequence from the PoC: a builder calls GET /api/global/self/api_key to mint a personal API key, then within minutes POSTs to /api/public/v1/roles/assign carrying builder:true or admin:true. The temporal pair from the same source identity / IP is a much stronger signal than either request alone and survives even if the body is not logged. Rationale: The PoC explicitly sequences GET /api/global/self/api_key (Step 2) and POST /api/public/v1/roles/assign (Step 3) from the same actor. The pair within a short window is far more specific than either request in isolation — legitimate admin UIs do not typically mint a personal API key and immediately use it against the public privilege-assignment endpoint. Corroborated against the GHSA advisory PoC and Budibase user-API documentation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6xp4-cf37-ppjh • https://docs.budibase.com/docs/public-api
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1098 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A genuine global admin testing the API workflow end-to-end after enabling the Enterprise public API
  • CI integration tests in a non-production tenant exercising the public role-assign endpoint
  • Vendor-side support engineer reproducing a customer issue via the documented PoC
  • Penetration-test engagement explicitly probing the GHSA-6xp4-cf37-ppjh fix
  • Internal red-team rotation key validation runs
Suppression filter
| where User !in~ (dynamic(["<break-glass-admin>", "<terraform-svc>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user owning the cIP / csUserName pair and check the BEFORE state of their builder/admin globals via the Budibase admin export. If they were workspace-scoped (builder.apps set, builder.global unset, admin.global unset) at mint time, treat as exploitation. 2) Contain: revoke the API key from /api/global/users/<id>/api_key, force a session reset for the implicated user, downgrade builder.global / admin.global on any userIds named in the assign body, and ensure @budibase/server is patched to >= 3.39.0. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same source IP for prior reconnaissance hits to /api/public/v1/applications, audit any datasource / automation / SCIM-OIDC config changes made under any account that became admin.global=true in the same window, and review SSO sign-in logs for the actor's tenant-admin access since the escalation.
// Budibase CVE-2026-48150 exploitation chain — API key minted then public roles/assign called within 30 min

    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project AssignTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl

| where AssignTime between (MintTime .. MintTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', AssignTime, MintTime)
| project MintTime, AssignTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl
| order by AssignTime desc

China-Linked Hackers Backdoored Linux Login Software to Hide for Nearly a Decade

Sygnia, which tracks the group as Velvet Ant, says it backdoored the PAM and OpenSSH components that decide who is allowed to sign in, planting its access where ordinary cleanup could not reach it. PAM Module File Modification on Linux Login Stack (Velvet Ant Operation Highland) AIInstallation High
Hunts unauthorised modification or replacement of PAM authentication modules (pam_unix.so, pam_sshd.so, pam_tally2.so) outside of legitimate package-manager activity. Velvet Ant replaced the main PAM login module with backdoored copies that accept secret passwords and harvest credentials. Rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'replaced the main PAM login module with backdoored copies' and that 'researchers found nine separate versions' — direct file-write to canonical PAM paths outside package management is the highest-fidelity primitive. Sygnia's Velvet Ant tracker corroborates PAM tampering as a recurring TTP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/china-nexus-threat-group-velvet-ant/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1556/003/
ATT&CKT1556.003 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised PAM module updates via custom deployment tools (Ansible, Salt, Puppet) not on the package-manager allowlist
  • Custom-built PAM modules (Duo, RSA SecurID, FreeIPA) deployed via tarball
  • In-place SSSD or SELinux policy upgrades that touch /usr/lib64/security
  • Security-tool agents (CrowdStrike, Tanium) replacing PAM hooks during install
  • Hand-applied vendor hotfix replacing pam_unix.so out-of-band
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible","salt-minion","puppet","chef-client","cfengine","falcon-sensor","tanium-client")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull SHA256 of the new module and compare to the package-manager's expected hash (`rpm -V pam` / `debsums pam-modules`). Identify the writing process, parent chain, and user — was it root via a known config-mgmt tool? 2. Contain: isolate the host from the network at the EDR layer; do NOT reset passwords yet (article warns the backdoor will capture the new ones). Snapshot the host for forensics; preserve /var/log/auth.log and /var/log/secure. 3. Hunt: pivot on the writing-process hash + parent across the fleet; check for sibling sshd/ssh binary writes within ±72h; review web-server access logs on internet-facing hosts for the staging webshell described in the article.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in ((DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform has "Linux" | distinct DeviceId))
| where FolderPath has_any ("/lib/security/","/lib64/security/","/usr/lib/security/","/usr/lib64/security/","/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/")
    or FileName in~ ("pam_unix.so","pam_sshd.so","pam_tally2.so","pam_deny.so","pam_permit.so","pam_env.so")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","zypper","unattended-upgrade","packagekitd","snapd","systemd")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/usr/lib/apt/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, PreviousFolderPath, PreviousFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in ("auth","authpriv","daemon","user")
| where SyslogMessage has "type=PATH"
   and (SyslogMessage has "pam_unix.so" or SyslogMessage has "pam_sshd.so" or SyslogMessage has "/lib/security/" or SyslogMessage has "/lib64/security/" or SyslogMessage has "/usr/lib/security/" or SyslogMessage has "/usr/lib64/security/")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("nametype=CREATE","nametype=NORMAL","nametype=DELETE")

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
