OpenSSH Binary or Crypto Library Modified Outside Package Update (Velvet Ant Operation Highland) AIInstallation High
Detects modification, replacement, or rename of /usr/sbin/sshd, /usr/bin/ssh, /usr/bin/scp or their linked libraries (libcrypto, libssl) outside of legitimate package-manager activity. Velvet Ant altered OpenSSH the same way as PAM to log credentials and every command typed, with a hidden switch to disable logging. Rationale: Article: 'OpenSSH programs were altered the same way, logging credentials and every command typed.' Targeting sshd/ssh/scp + their linked crypto libs covers the trojaned-binary primitive directly. Sygnia's earlier Velvet Ant reporting and MITRE T1554 reinforce this is the actor's preferred persistence mechanism. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/china-nexus-threat-group-velvet-ant/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1554/
ATT&CKT1554 T1556
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • OpenSSH source-build upgrade installing via `make install` instead of package manager
  • Hardening tools (Lynis, OpenSCAP remediation) replacing sshd binary
  • DevOps custom OpenSSH builds with FIPS patches deployed via tarball
  • Container image baking process writing sshd into rootfs overlays
  • Vendor-supplied hotfix tarball during emergency CVE response
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "make install" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible","salt-minion","puppet","chef-client","oscap")
Response runbook
1. Triage: compute SHA256 of the new binary and compare to distro package hash (`rpm -qf /usr/sbin/sshd` then `rpm -V`); inspect the writing process tree and the writing user's logon source. 2. Contain: network-isolate the host; do NOT restart sshd or reset credentials (the backdoor will capture replacements). Capture memory and the on-disk binary; verify against a known-good copy from the vendor mirror before any replacement. 3. Hunt: query the same writer hash across the fleet; check for sibling pam_*.so writes within ±72h; review auth.log for sshd accepting unusual usernames or empty password fields; pivot to internet-facing web servers for the staging bridge described in the article.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in ((DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform has "Linux" | distinct DeviceId))
| where FolderPath in~ ("/usr/sbin/sshd","/usr/bin/ssh","/usr/bin/scp","/usr/bin/sftp","/usr/bin/ssh-agent","/usr/bin/ssh-keygen")
    or (FolderPath has_any ("/usr/lib64/","/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/","/lib64/") and FileName matches regex @"^lib(crypto|ssl)\.so(\.[0-9]+)*$")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","zypper","unattended-upgrade","packagekitd","snapd","ldconfig")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, PreviousFolderPath, PreviousFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in ("auth","authpriv","daemon","user","kern")
| where SyslogMessage has "type=PATH"
   and (SyslogMessage has "/usr/sbin/sshd" or SyslogMessage has "/usr/bin/ssh" or SyslogMessage has "/usr/bin/scp" or SyslogMessage has "/usr/bin/sftp" or SyslogMessage has "libcrypto.so" or SyslogMessage has "libssl.so")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("nametype=CREATE","nametype=NORMAL","nametype=DELETE")
| where not(SyslogMessage has_any ("exe=\"/usr/bin/dpkg\"","exe=\"/usr/bin/rpm\"","exe=\"/usr/bin/apt\"","exe=\"/usr/bin/yum\"","exe=\"/usr/bin/dnf\"","exe=\"/usr/lib/apt/apt-helper\"","exe=\"/sbin/ldconfig\"","comm=\"unattended-upgr\""))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SSHD Process Writes to Non-Standard Path (Hidden Credential Log File) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects sshd writing to atypical paths — /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, hidden dotfiles — strongly suggestive of the credential-logging behaviour of Velvet Ant's trojaned OpenSSH. Legitimate sshd writes only to its known config/runtime locations. Rationale: Article describes the trojaned sshd 'quietly recorded real usernames and passwords as people logged in' — a logger needs a sink. sshd writing to /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm or a hidden file is anomalous against the legitimate write set (/var/log, /var/run, /etc/ssh). Cross-checked against: • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/china-nexus-threat-group-velvet-ant/
ATT&CKT1056.001 T1003.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • sshd debug builds writing trace logs to /tmp during troubleshooting
  • sshd ChrootDirectory pointing into a non-standard prefix
  • SELinux audit relabel temporarily redirecting sshd writes
  • Custom MOTD scripts invoked via sshd ForceCommand creating temp files
  • Container-init sshd writing pid/socket files to non-default runtime dir
Response runbook
1. Triage: read the file Velocity wrote — if it contains plaintext credentials, username+IP pairs, or session transcripts, the binary is compromised. Hash the sshd binary and compare to distro known-good. 2. Contain: isolate the host; preserve the captured-credentials file and the sshd binary for forensics; treat every user who logged in since the file's mtime as credential-exposed. 3. Hunt: look for sibling sshd writes across the fleet at the same path; correlate with outbound SSH/SCP from this host (attacker may exfil the log); review auth.log for the secret-password authentications described in the article (successful logins with no key + no PAM challenge).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in ((DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform has "Linux" | distinct DeviceId))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sshd"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath startswith "/var/tmp/" or FolderPath startswith "/dev/shm/"
    or (FileName startswith "." and FolderPath !startswith "/root/.ssh" and FolderPath !startswith "/home/" and FolderPath !startswith "/etc/ssh")
| where FolderPath !startswith "/var/log"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in ("auth","authpriv")
| where SyslogMessage has "type=PATH"
   and SyslogMessage has "exe=\"/usr/sbin/sshd\""
   and (SyslogMessage has "name=\"/tmp/" or SyslogMessage has "name=\"/var/tmp/" or SyslogMessage has "name=\"/dev/shm/")
   and (SyslogMessage has "nametype=CREATE" or SyslogMessage has "nametype=NORMAL")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, Facility, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Internet-Facing Web Server Spawns SSH or Shell into Internal Segment AICommand & Control High
Hunts the Velvet Ant 'bridge' pattern: internet-facing web server (httpd, nginx, tomcat, apache2) spawning ssh/scp/bash/nc to an internal IP — the relay mechanism used to reach the air-gapped network that hosted the backdoored login software. Rationale: Article: 'the attacker used... an internet-facing web server as a bridge, passing commands through it to open remote sessions deep inside the segment that had no direct internet access.' Web-server-parented ssh/bash to RFC1918 is the exact bridge primitive and rare in clean environments. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/china-nexus-threat-group-velvet-ant/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/002/
ATT&CKT1090.002 T1505.003 T1021.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Application-tier health check shelling out to ssh for cluster status
  • CI/CD agent (Jenkins worker) running under nginx user proxying deploys to backends
  • WordPress/Drupal cron tasks invoking curl/wget to internal services
  • Backup utility triggered from a web admin panel running scp/rsync
  • Custom monitoring webhook running socat as a TCP proxy
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "/healthcheck" and ProcessCommandLine !has "jenkins"
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the command line and RFC1918 destination; identify the destination host and whether it sits in a segment the web server has no legitimate reason to reach. Inspect the web server's recent access logs for the request that triggered the spawn (look for unfamiliar paths and POST bodies). 2. Contain: kill the spawned process; block the source web server's egress to the internal segment at the firewall/NSG; preserve the web-server root directory for webshell forensics. 3. Hunt: pivot on the destination IP for inbound SSH from this host across the fleet; look for sibling pam_*.so / sshd writes on the destination host within ±72h; check F5 BIG-IP appliances for unexpected outbound connections per the article's prior-case note.
let DmzHosts = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | where IsInternetFacing == true and OSPlatform has "Linux"
    | distinct DeviceId;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in (DmzHosts)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("httpd","nginx","apache2","java","tomcat","php-fpm","node","python","python3","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("ssh","scp","sftp","bash","sh","nc","ncat","socat","curl","wget","chisel","frpc","ligolo")
| where AccountName !in~ ("root")
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any (" 10."," 172.16."," 172.17."," 172.18."," 172.19."," 172.20."," 172.21."," 172.22."," 172.23."," 172.24."," 172.25."," 172.26."," 172.27."," 172.28."," 172.29."," 172.30."," 172.31."," 192.168.")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let DmzHosts = DeviceInfo
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | where IsInternetFacing == true and OSPlatform has "Linux"
    | distinct DeviceName;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname in (DmzHosts) or DvcHostname has_any (DmzHosts)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("httpd","nginx","apache2","java","tomcat","php-fpm","node","python")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("ssh","scp","sftp","bash","sh","nc","ncat","socat","chisel","frpc","ligolo")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (" 10."," 172.16."," 172.17."," 172.18."," 172.19."," 172.20."," 172.21."," 172.22."," 172.23."," 172.24."," 172.25."," 172.26."," 172.27."," 172.28."," 172.29."," 172.30."," 172.31."," 192.168.")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cisco NX-OS CVE-2024-20399 Post-Auth Bash Container Escape (Velvet Ant Persistence) AIExploitation Medium
Detects exploitation of CVE-2024-20399 on Cisco Nexus switches — authenticated admin invoking `run bash` or piping shell metacharacters through configuration commands to escape the NX-OS CLI and execute root commands on the underlying Linux. Velvet Ant used this to plant switch-resident backdoors. Rationale: Article links the same actor to CVE-2024-20399 ('plant a backdoor on the switches') — Cisco PSIRT details that the bug allows escape from the restricted NX-OS CLI to underlying bash via command-injection in select CLI commands by an authenticated admin. Detection targets the injection metacharacters and the bash-shell feature, which is the actor's foothold primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-nxos-cmd-injection-xD9OhyOP • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/china-nexus-threat-group-velvet-ant/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1068 T1542.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised TAC troubleshooting using `run bash` for live diagnostics
  • Network automation tooling (Ansible cisco.nxos modules) using shell-out for config inspection
  • Legitimate `feature bash-shell` enablement during platform upgrade planning
  • Operator copy-paste containing semicolons or backticks in description fields
  • NX-API REST sessions where command output text contains shell metacharacters
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the invoking admin via TACACS+/RADIUS accounting; verify the device is on a patched NX-OS train (Cisco patched July 2024 — anything older is exposed). Inspect bash-shell session for downloaded binaries or modified /etc/init.d, /isan/, /bootflash entries. 2. Contain: revoke the admin credentials used; suspend network-admin AAA group; capture `show tech` and bootflash image for forensics; do NOT reload (some implants live only in memory and an image-verify will be the diagnostic). 3. Hunt: cross-check bootflash image hash against Cisco's published SHA512; query other Nexus gear for the same admin running `run bash`; correlate with internet-facing F5 BIG-IP outbound activity per the prior Sygnia case the article references.
union isfuzzy=true 
(Syslog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where ProcessName has_any ("VSHD","AAA","SECURITYD") or SyslogMessage has "CMD_EXEC_LOGD"),
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DeviceVendor has "Cisco" and DeviceProduct has_any ("NX-OS","Nexus"))
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("run bash","feature bash-shell","|sh","| sh","$(", "; rm ","; wget","; curl","`")
   or Message has_any ("run bash","feature bash-shell","|sh","| sh","$(")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SourceUserName=coalesce(column_ifexists("SourceUserName",""),""), Cmd=coalesce(SyslogMessage, Message)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:cisco.nxos (@message:*"run bash"* OR @message:*"feature bash-shell"* OR @message:*"|sh"* OR @message:*"$("* OR @message:*"; rm "* OR @message:*"; wget"* OR @message:*"; curl"*)
APPLICATION
`cisco_nxos` | search (message="*run bash*" OR message="*; *" OR message="*| sh*" OR message="*$(" OR message="*`*" OR message="*feature bash-shell*") AND (message="*configure*" OR message="*show*" OR message="*python*") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(user) as users values(message) as cmds by host | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)

| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)

| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

DeviceProcessEvents

SecurityEvent

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Atomic Arch — pacman/makepkg post-install spawning npm install of atomic-lockfile AIInstallation High
Detects the install-time pivot of the Atomic Arch supply-chain campaign: a pacman/makepkg PKGBUILD post-install hook spawning npm or node to fetch the malicious atomic-lockfile package. The combination of an Arch package-build parent with an npm child referencing atomic-lockfile is specific to this campaign and absent from clean AUR installs. Rationale: atomic-lockfile is the named malicious npm package both IFIN and Sonatype identified as the second-stage payload of the Atomic Arch campaign. Pacman/makepkg are the only legitimate Arch package-build parents — they should never spawn npm referencing this string. Cross-checked with Sonatype's writeup on the AUR PKGBUILD post-install hook. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://www.sonatype.com/blog • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.004 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate AUR maintainer publishing a benign package literally named atomic-lockfile or with that string in a dependency (none currently exist on npm)
  • Developer manually invoking npm install atomic-lockfile while researching this campaign
  • Security team running validation tests against the IOC
  • SBOM/dependency-audit tools that enumerate package names in logs
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dry-run","--audit-only")) and not(AccountName in~ ("securityresearch","detectiondev"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the host installed an AUR package in the preceding 10 minutes via /var/log/pacman.log; identify the trojanized PKGBUILD owner and capture the SHA256 of the npm-dropped ELF. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the workstation from the network, kill the npm/node descendant process tree, and snapshot /tmp, ~/.npm, and ~/.cache for forensics before reimaging. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the developer's identity — rotate GitHub PATs, npm tokens, SSH keys, HashiCorp Vault tokens, and any Slack/Teams/Discord refresh tokens; search org-wide for other hosts installing the same AUR package name in the last 30 days; check DNS for temp.sh and any .onion resolution attempts from the affected subnet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("makepkg","pacman","bash","sh","zsh")
| where FileName has_any ("npm","node","pnpm","yarn","npx")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "atomic-lockfile"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "atomic-lockfile"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("makepkg","pacman","PKGBUILD")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("npm"," node ","pnpm","yarn","npx")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Atomic Arch — Pacman/Makepkg Spawns NPM Install of atomic-lockfile
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7081-9203-4567890abcde
description: Detects pacman or makepkg parent spawning an npm/node child that references the malicious atomic-lockfile package distributed by the Atomic Arch AUR supply-chain compromise.

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(makepkg|pacman|bash|sh|zsh)$/i ImageFileName=/(npm|node|pnpm|yarn|npx)$/i

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Atomic Arch — ELF payload 'deps' written or executed under build/cache directories after AUR install AIInstallation High
Detects creation or execution of the ELF infostealer 'deps' dropped by the atomic-lockfile npm package, identified by its specific SHA256/MD5 and by the file name 'deps' landing in npm/build/cache directories shortly after an AUR install. This is the second-stage payload that performs credential harvesting. Rationale: SHA256 6144d433...3c98b and MD5 42b59fdb...bf40 are the article's pre-extracted IOCs for the 'deps' ELF infostealer. The filename 'deps' under npm/build/cache dirs is the secondary heuristic for variants of the same dropper where the hash has been recompiled. Cross-checked with the IFIN/Whanos report referenced in the article and MITRE T1204.002. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate npm package shipping a binary called 'deps' as part of its build (some Go/Rust toolchains do this — verify by hash, not name alone)
  • Developer manually saving a hash-matching file from a research/sandbox
  • Security tooling that imports IOC sets into local test corpora
  • CI runners that bundle node_modules including binary helpers
Suppression filter
| where not(FolderPath has_any ("/go/pkg/mod/","/cargo/registry/") and FileName == "deps")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the hash match; if name-only, compute and compare the actual SHA256 against the IOC. Pull pacman.log to identify the AUR package whose post-install triggered the npm fetch. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, terminate any running 'deps' process and its npm/node parent chain, preserve the binary and the npm cache for malware reverse-engineering. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep org-wide for the SHA256/MD5 IOCs and for any 'deps' ELF in user cache dirs; pivot on the maintainer alias on the affected AUR package and check if other PKGBUILDs from arojas, krisztinavarga, custodiatovar, or veramagalhaes were installed.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where SHA256 == "6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b"
   or MD5 == "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"
   or (FileName == "deps" and FolderPath has_any ("/.cache/", "/.npm/", "/build/", "/tmp/", "/node_modules/"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, FileSize, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b","42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40")
   or (SyslogMessage has "name=\"deps\"" and SyslogMessage has_any ("/.cache/","/.npm/","/build/","/tmp/","/node_modules/"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Atomic Arch rootkit — eBPF program load by AUR-build-chain descendant AIInstallation Medium
Detects loading of an eBPF program by a process whose ancestor chain includes pacman/makepkg/npm/node or the 'deps' ELF — the privilege-escalation step of the Atomic Arch rootkit. Legitimate eBPF users (systemd, kubelet, cilium, bpftool) are excluded; the campaign uses bpf() syscalls to install a kernel-resident process/file/network hider. Rationale: The article explicitly states the malware uses eBPF for kernel-level execution and hiding ("the malware can run inside the kernel with elevated privileges and hide local processes"). bpf() syscall and BPF_PROG_LOAD are the auditd-visible signals of eBPF loading. Restricting the ancestor chain to pacman/makepkg/npm/node/deps removes legitimate eBPF users. Falcon LogScale left empty — FDR doesn't ship a dedicated bpf-syscall event in the documented schema. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1014/ • https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/bpf/
ATT&CKT1068 T1014 T1547
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer on an Arch host running bcc/bpftrace/perf tools manually for performance work
  • tcpdump or wireshark loading XDP/BPF socket filters under sudo
  • Newly-installed eBPF-using observability agents (Pixie, Parca, Inspektor Gadget) on dev boxes
  • Container runtimes other than the excluded set (podman with seccomp BPF) when started from a shell
  • Cilium or other CNI plugins running outside their normal service path during debugging
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bpftrace","bcc-tools","perf record","tcpdump","bpftool"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the loading process and its full ancestor chain; if rooted at pacman/makepkg, this is almost certainly malicious. Capture `bpftool prog show` and `bpftool map show` output and snapshot /sys/fs/bpf. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host immediately — an eBPF rootkit can hide processes from EDR. Reboot to a known-good kernel/initrd and image the disk before wiping. Step 3 (hunt): Compare userland `ps`/`ss`/`ls /proc` against kernel-visible lists via auditd or `/proc/<pid>/status` directly; alert on discrepancies. Sweep org for any host with eBPF programs persisted across reboots that aren't owned by a known service.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("BpfProgramLoaded","SyscallAudit","EBPFActivity")
   or AdditionalFields has_any ("BPF_PROG_LOAD","sys_bpf","CAP_BPF","type=BPF")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("systemd","systemd-bpf","kubelet","cilium-agent","bpftool","containerd","dockerd","falcon-sensor","runc")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("pacman","makepkg","npm","node","sh","bash")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName == "deps"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("atomic-lockfile","/deps")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in~ ("auth","authpriv","user","kern","daemon") or ProcessName has_any ("auditd","kauditd","audisp")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("BPF_PROG_LOAD","type=BPF","CAP_BPF","sys_bpf","syscall=321")
| where not(SyslogMessage has_any ("systemd","kubelet","cilium","bpftool","containerd","dockerd","falcon-sensor","runc"))
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("pacman","makepkg","npm"," node ","atomic-lockfile","/deps","comm=\"deps\"")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:BPF OR @auditd.syscall:bpf OR @process.command_line:(*BPF_PROG_LOAD* OR *sys_bpf*)) -@process.executable.path:(*\/systemd* OR *\/kubelet OR *\/cilium* OR *\/bpftool OR *\/containerd OR *\/dockerd OR *\/falcon-sensor)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process_name values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*BPF_PROG_LOAD*" OR Processes.process="*bpf(*" OR Processes.process="*sys_bpf*" OR Processes.process="*CAP_BPF*") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("pacman","makepkg","npm","node","sh","bash","deps") AND NOT Processes.process_name IN ("systemd","kubelet","cilium-agent","bpftool","containerd","dockerd") by host Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process_name values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*BPF_PROG_LOAD*" OR Processes.process="*bpf(*" OR Processes.process="*sys_bpf*" OR Processes.process="*CAP_BPF*") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("pacman","makepkg","npm","node","sh","bash","deps") AND NOT Processes.process_name IN ("systemd","kubelet","cilium-agent","bpftool","containerd","dockerd") by host Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Atomic Arch infostealer — bulk reads of SSH/npmrc/Vault/browser-cookie files by non-shell process AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the Atomic Arch 'deps' ELF (or any non-legitimate process) reading multiple credential files in sequence: ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.vault-token, browser cookie SQLite DBs, and Slack/Teams/Discord local stores. The fan-out across these specific paths from a single short-lived process is the campaign's credential-harvesting signature. Rationale: Whanos' analysis (cited in the article) enumerates the exact set of credential stores 'deps' targets: GitHub/npm tokens, SSH artifacts, HashiCorp Vault tokens, browser cookies, Slack/Teams/Discord/Telegram data, Docker/Podman config, shell histories. Detecting a non-legit process that reads four or more of these in a short window is far more specific than any single-file watch. Cross-checked Sonatype's binary-string list against the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dotfile-sync tools (yadm, chezmoi, stow) iterating over ~/.ssh + ~/.npmrc + ~/.docker on first run
  • Backup agents (restic, borg, duplicity, BorgBase) reading user home as part of a scheduled snapshot
  • Indexers like Tracker3/Recoll/baloo touching all user files including credential stores
  • DevSecOps secret scanners run manually (trufflehog, gitleaks, semgrep secrets)
  • Migration scripts moving a user profile between hosts
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("yadm","chezmoi","stow","restic","borg","duplicity","tracker-miner-fs-3","baloo_file","trufflehog","gitleaks"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the reading process binary — if it's the 'deps' ELF or any unsigned binary under ~/.npm, ~/.cache, or /tmp, treat as confirmed. Snapshot the process's open file descriptors and network connections via /proc. Step 2 (contain): Kill the process tree, isolate the host, immediately revoke all credentials whose files were touched: rotate SSH keys, regenerate GitHub PATs and npm tokens, revoke and re-issue HashiCorp Vault tokens, force browser cookie invalidation, and reset Slack/Teams/Discord sessions. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the SSH keys' authorized_keys distribution across the fleet; check GitHub audit log for new SSH-key uploads or PAT creations from the user; check Vault audit log for token-use from unusual IPs; sweep for the same process binary on other developer workstations.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRead","FileOpened","FileAccessed","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/.ssh/", "/.npmrc", "/.docker/config.json", "/.vault-token", "/.config/Slack/", "/.config/discord/", "/.config/Microsoft/Teams/", "/.mozilla/firefox/", "/snap/firefox", "/.config/google-chrome/", "/.config/chromium/")
   or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","cookies.sqlite","Cookies","Login Data",".vault-token",".npmrc")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sshd","ssh","scp","sftp","ssh-agent","gpg-agent","git","firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","slack","teams","discord","keepassxc","gnome-keyring-d","systemd","systemd-user","cron","tar","rsync","backup")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), DistinctPaths=dcount(FolderPath), SamplePaths=make_set(FolderPath, 20), SampleFiles=make_set(FileName, 20) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| where DistinctPaths >= 4
| order by FirstSeen desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in~ ("auth","authpriv","user") or ProcessName has_any ("auditd","kauditd")
| extend SensitivePath = case(
    SyslogMessage has "/.ssh/id_", "ssh_key",
    SyslogMessage has "/.npmrc", "npmrc",
    SyslogMessage has "/.docker/config.json", "docker_cfg",
    SyslogMessage has ".vault-token", "vault_token",
    SyslogMessage has "/.config/Slack", "slack",
    SyslogMessage has "/.config/discord", "discord",
    SyslogMessage has "/Microsoft/Teams", "teams",
    SyslogMessage has "cookies.sqlite", "browser_cookies",
    SyslogMessage has "Login Data", "browser_login",
    "")
| where isnotempty(SensitivePath)
| where not(SyslogMessage has_any ("comm=\"ssh\"","comm=\"sshd\"","comm=\"gpg-agent\"","comm=\"firefox\"","comm=\"chrome\"","comm=\"slack\"","comm=\"teams\"","comm=\"discord\"","comm=\"keepassxc\""))
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), DistinctPaths=dcount(SensitivePath), Paths=make_set(SensitivePath) by Computer, HostName, ProcessName
| where DistinctPaths >= 4
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(SYSCALL OR PATH) @file.path:(*\/.ssh\/id_* OR *\/.npmrc OR *\/.docker\/config.json OR *\/.vault-token OR *\/.config\/Slack\/* OR *\/.config\/discord\/* OR *\/Microsoft\/Teams\/* OR *cookies.sqlite OR *"Login Data"*) -@process.name:(ssh OR sshd OR scp OR sftp OR firefox OR chrome OR chromium OR brave OR slack OR teams OR discord OR keepassxc OR gpg-agent OR git)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo (regex("/\\.ssh/id_", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/\\.npmrc$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/\\.docker/config\\.json$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/\\.vault-token$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/\\.config/(Slack|discord)/", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/Microsoft/Teams/", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("cookies\\.sqlite$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/Login Data$", field=TargetFileName))
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/(ssh|sshd|scp|sftp|firefox|chrome|chromium|brave|slack|teams|discord|keepassxc|gpg-agent|git)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctPaths))
| DistinctPaths >= 4
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/known_hosts" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.vault-token" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/Slack/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/discord/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Microsoft/Teams/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/cookies.sqlite" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Login Data") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("ssh","sshd","ssh-agent","scp","sftp","gpg-agent","git","firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","slack","teams","discord","keepassxc","gnome-keyring-d") by host Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user bin(_time,5m) | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 4
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/known_hosts" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.vault-token" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/Slack/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/discord/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Microsoft/Teams/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/cookies.sqlite" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Login Data") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("ssh","sshd","ssh-agent","scp","sftp","gpg-agent","git","firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","slack","teams","discord","keepassxc","gnome-keyring-d") by host Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user bin(_time,5m) | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 4
Atomic Arch — DNS resolution and HTTP POST to temp.sh from non-browser developer workstation process AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS lookups for temp.sh and HTTP/HTTPS uploads to temp.sh originating from non-browser processes — the Atomic Arch campaign's primary clearnet exfil channel. Browsers/curl-from-shell are noisy on this domain but the 'deps' ELF or an npm/node descendant uploading to it is the campaign signature. Rationale: temp.sh is the article's pre-extracted clearnet exfil domain. Whanos' report and the IFIN summary both flag it as the file-host destination for the archived credential bundles. The non-browser process filter is essential because temp.sh has legitimate human users — the differentiator is that 'deps'/npm/node/curl-from-cron should never POST there from a developer workstation. Cross-checked the .onion + temp.sh dual-channel pattern in the Sonatype writeup. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/ • https://temp.sh/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually uploading a debug log or screenshot to temp.sh via curl/wget for sharing
  • CI/CD job that posts artifacts to temp.sh as part of a lightweight share workflow
  • Security researcher fetching the IOC sample itself from temp.sh for analysis
  • Misconfigured backup script using temp.sh as a poor-man's file drop
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ci-artifact","DEBUG_SHARE","researcher-sandbox"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full URL path of the POST and the SentBytes to estimate payload size; if multi-MB and the host installed an AUR package in the last 24h, treat as confirmed exfil. Step 2 (contain): Block temp.sh at egress, isolate the host, and pull any temp.sh download URLs the operator may use to retrieve. If the upload URL is recoverable, GET it to capture what was exfiltrated. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep the org for other workstations resolving temp.sh in the last 30 days; correlate with AUR install timestamps from pacman.log; rotate every credential the deps stealer targets (SSH, GitHub, npm, Vault, browser, Slack/Teams/Discord) for any affected user.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "temp.sh" or RemoteUrl endswith ".temp.sh"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome","firefox","msedge","safari","brave","chromium","opera")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let TempShDNS = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Name has "temp.sh"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Source="DNS";
let TempShHTTP = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DestinationHostName has "temp.sh" or RequestURL has "temp.sh"
    | where isnotempty(ProcessName) and ProcessName !in~ ("firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","msedge","safari")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Name=DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, SentBytes, ProcessName, Source="Proxy";
union isfuzzy=true TempShDNS, TempShHTTP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Atomic Arch — Exfil HTTP POST to temp.sh by Non-Browser Process

      - /brave

(source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog) (@network.destination.host:*temp.sh* OR @dns.question.name:*temp.sh*) -@process.name:(firefox OR chrome OR chromium OR brave OR safari OR msedge)

| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/temp\.sh$/i | groupBy([aid], function={ collect([DomainName]) })}, field=aid)

Atomic Arch — Tor client spawn or .onion endpoint contact from AUR-installing developer host AICommand & Control High
Detects Tor client/daemon process execution or attempted resolution/contact of the campaign's specific .onion endpoint on hosts that recently installed AUR packages. Tor on a developer workstation is unusual baseline; pairing with the AUR-install context isolates the campaign's hidden-service C2 channel. Rationale: The article and IFIN/Whanos report cite olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion as the Tor hidden-service C2 — that specific 56-char v3 onion string is the campaign's fingerprint. Tor client spawn on a developer workstation that just ran an AUR install is high-fidelity by itself; literal-onion matches are unambiguous. Cross-checked the dual-channel exfil pattern in the Sonatype report. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/003/
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running Tor Browser for personal privacy reasons on a BYOD-permitted workstation
  • Researcher analyzing this campaign and resolving the onion address in a sandbox
  • Whistleblower-tooling installations (SecureDrop client) on journalism-focused dev hosts
  • onionshare or similar legitimate file-sharing tooling tested by a user
Suppression filter
| where not(AccountName in~ ("securityresearch","detectiondev") and ProcessCommandLine has "sandbox")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): If the matched string is the literal campaign onion, this is a confirmed C2 contact — escalate immediately. For generic Tor process spawns, check parent chain for pacman/makepkg/npm/node ancestry to disambiguate from human Tor Browser use. Step 2 (contain): Block Tor egress at the firewall (block known Tor entry guards or DPI-block Tor protocol fingerprint), isolate the host, and capture full packet capture from the host's interface for forensics. Step 3 (hunt): Search 30 days back for any host org-wide that contacted the campaign onion or any Tor entry guard; cross-reference with the AUR-installing-host list from the pacman.log sweep; rotate every credential class the 'deps' stealer targets for the affected user.
let TorProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("tor","tor.real","torify","torsocks","obfs4proxy","snowflake-client")
       or ProcessCommandLine has_any (".onion","olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid","SocksPort","HiddenServiceDir")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256, Source="Process";
let OnionDNS = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has ".onion" or RemoteUrl has "olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256=InitiatingProcessSHA256, Source="Network";
union TorProcs, OnionDNS
| order by Timestamp desc
let TorDNS = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Name has_any (".onion","olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, Source="DNS";
let TorProc = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ProcessName in~ ("tor","torify","torsocks","obfs4proxy","snowflake-client")
       or SyslogMessage has_any (".onion","olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid","HiddenServiceDir","SocksPort")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, Source="Process";
union isfuzzy=true TorDNS, TorProc
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.

SecurityEvent

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40") or SHA1 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40") or MD5 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40") or SHA1 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40") or MD5 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
