OpenClaw agent runtime reads secrets store (.env / .aws / id_rsa) followed by external network egress AIActions on Objectives High
Detects an AI agent process opening a credential / secrets file then making an outbound connection to a public IP within 5 minutes. Article-specific: Varonis' Pinchy agent on OpenClaw was driven by a single phishing email to locate and forward mock AWS IAM keys, DB connection strings, and SSH credentials in plaintext. Rationale: Varonis showed OpenClaw's Pinchy agent forwarded AWS IAM keys, DB connection strings, and SSH credentials in response to one phishing email — the file-read-then-egress join uses the article's exact credential targets (.env / .aws / SSH keys) anchored to the agent process, with a 5-minute correlation window matching the typical agent prompt-to-action cadence. Cross-checked against: • https://www.varonis.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1041/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1005 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developers running `aws sts get-caller-identity` or `terraform plan` from a Python venv that reads .aws/credentials then talks to public AWS endpoints
  • CI bootstrap scripts (python/node) that read .env then post telemetry to Datadog / Sentry / Honeycomb
  • OpenClaw legitimately tasked to deploy infra (reads ~/.aws/credentials, then API call to AWS public IPs)
  • Git operations from agent-driven workflows reading id_rsa to push to github.com
  • Backup tools (Restic / BorgBackup) running under agent context reading config then uploading to S3
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("amazonaws.com","github.com","datadoghq.com","sentry.io") and ReadCmd has_any ("terraform","aws-cli","awscli","git push","ci-bootstrap"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the exact file path read and the destination IP/URL; resolve the destination against the org's known-good SaaS list (AWS / GitHub / known telemetry endpoints) and check whether the same agent has ever talked to that destination in the prior 30d. 2) Contain: revoke every credential type the agent read — rotate the AWS access key, regenerate the SSH key, expire DB connection strings, and disable the OpenClaw connector that handled the triggering message; preserve the agent's conversation log for forensics. 3) Hunt: query EmailEvents for inbound messages in the hour before the read that name credentials/keys/staging access (Varonis' Dan-the-team-lead pretext); pivot on the user object to find any other agent invocations they triggered; check for outbound EmailEvents from the same mailbox sending the credentials onward.
let SecretPaths = dynamic([@"\.env", @"\.aws\", @"\.ssh\", @"\.netrc", "credentials.json", "secrets.json", "id_rsa", "id_ed25519"]);
let AgentProcs = dynamic(["openclaw.exe","openclaw","python.exe","python3","node.exe","node"]);
let SecretReads = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FolderPath has_any (SecretPaths) or FileName has_any (SecretPaths)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any (AgentProcs)
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("openclaw","langchain","autogpt","agent.py")
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | project ReadTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              AccessedPath = strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName),
              ReadProcess  = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              ReadCmd      = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ReadAccount  = InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let Egress = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any (AgentProcs)
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("openclaw","langchain","autogpt","agent.py")
    | project EgressTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort;
SecretReads
| join kind=inner Egress on DeviceId
| where EgressTime between (ReadTime .. ReadTime + 5m)
| project ReadTime, EgressTime,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', EgressTime, ReadTime),
          DeviceName, ReadAccount, AccessedPath, ReadProcess, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl
| order by ReadTime desc

let SecretReads = ImFileEvent

let Egress = ImNetworkSession

    | where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "172."
    | where SrcUsername !endswith "$"
    | project EgressTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber;
SecretReads
| join kind=inner Egress on DvcHostname
| where EgressTime between (ReadTime .. ReadTime + 5m)
| project ReadTime, EgressTime,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', EgressTime, ReadTime),
          DvcHostname, ReadAccount, AccessedPath, ReadProcess, DstIpAddr, DstHostname
| order by ReadTime desc

Outbound connection or DNS resolution to imperva_artifactory.com (OpenClaw PoC C2) AICommand & Control High
Hunts for any host in the estate resolving or connecting to imperva_artifactory.com, the researcher-controlled C2 named in Imperva's OpenClaw prompt-injection PoC. Hits indicate either an Imperva-affiliated test, an unpatched OpenClaw instance still triggering the PoC, or a copycat using the same payload. Rationale: imperva_artifactory.com is the only hard IOC in the article — Imperva's researcher-controlled server used to host the PoC payload. Any hit is either an Imperva test, an unpatched OpenClaw running the public PoC, or a copycat — all three are worth a ticket. Low FP because the domain is non-generic and not a legitimate Imperva product domain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.imperva.com/blog/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-attacks-trick-openclaw-ai-agent.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red team / purple team replicating the Imperva PoC against the org's own OpenClaw instance
  • Imperva-internal hosts if the org uses Imperva products and Imperva pivots from corp infra
  • Security researchers in the org clicking through the article's IOC links from a managed device
  • Threat-intel feed enrichment platforms pre-fetching the domain for reputation scoring
  • WAF / proxy products doing DNS-pre-resolve on URLs seen in inbound article-link emails
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the process and user that initiated the resolution/connection; if the initiating process matches an AI agent runtime (openclaw / python / node / langchain), treat as confirmed PoC execution. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the agent process, snapshot the agent's conversation log, block imperva_artifactory.com at the DNS / web proxy / firewall layer estate-wide, and verify OpenClaw version is ≥2026.4.23 (the patched build). 3) Hunt: pivot on the agent's user / mailbox / WhatsApp connector to identify the originating shared-contact or vCard whose name field carried the prompt injection — Imperva's article describes the `<contact: name, number>` payload shape; quarantine the source contact and notify any other internal users it was shared with.
let Indicator = "imperva_artifactory.com";
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceNetworkEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where RemoteUrl has Indicator
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source="NetworkEvents"),
  (DeviceEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
   | where AdditionalFields has Indicator or RemoteUrl has Indicator
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source="DeviceEvents")
| order by Timestamp desc
let Indicator = "imperva_artifactory.com";
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has Indicator
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, Source="ImDnsActivity"),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has Indicator
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryTypeName, Source="DnsEvents"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has Indicator or DestinationHostName has Indicator
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DeviceVendor, Source="CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Network Resolution or Connection to imperva_artifactory.com (OpenClaw PoC C2)

AI-agent-driven mailbox auto-forwards messages to first-time-seen external recipient AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects an internal mailbox (one connected to an AI agent like OpenClaw / Pinchy) sending mail to an external address the mailbox has never sent to before, within a short window of receiving an inbound message. Article-specific: Varonis showed Pinchy forwarded AWS keys and a 247-row customer dataset to outside addresses after one social-pretext email, even under a 'verify senders first' strict profile. Rationale: Varonis' Pinchy agent forwarded AWS IAM keys and a 247-customer export to external addresses after social-pretext emails — the article's central exfil pattern. First-time-recipient join against a 60-day baseline isolates the 'agent shipped data to a stranger' shape; correlating with a recent inbound message captures the 'one email triggers exfil' cadence Varonis demonstrated. Domain allowlist for gmail/outlook strips most personal-mail noise without losing the dedicated exfil-to-attacker case. Cross-checked against: • https://www.varonis.com/blog/ • https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jun/16/the-lethal-trifecta/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/003/
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1567 T1041
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sales / BD outreach where a rep emails a brand-new prospect after receiving an inbound RFQ within 30 minutes
  • Helpdesk responding to first-time external vendor support tickets
  • Recruiters mailing first-time candidates after receiving inbound applications
  • HR sending offer letters / NDAs to first-time external addresses after an inbound interview reply
  • Customer-support mailboxes (Zendesk-style) replying to first-time customer addresses within minutes
Suppression filter
| where not (MailboxOwner has_any ("sales","support","helpdesk","recruiting","hr-","noreply","no-reply","jobs","careers"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the outbound message body and attachments, then the inbound message that preceded it — assess whether the outbound contains credentials (AWS keys, DB strings, SSH keys), a customer / CRM export, or any structured secret payload Varonis described; confirm the mailbox is wired to an OpenClaw / agent connector. 2) Contain: disable the agent's outbound-mail capability and the mailbox auto-forward / inbox rules, recall the outbound message via M365 admin, and block the external recipient domain at the mail-flow layer if it looks attacker-controlled. 3) Hunt: review the same mailbox for any other first-time external sends in the last 30d, look for inbound 'urgency' / 'incident' / 'QBR' / 'export' keywords that match Varonis' Dan-pretext or weekly-customer-export pretext, and validate the agent's instruction file is version-controlled and includes the strict 'verify sender first + human-in-the-loop for credentials' guardrail Varonis recommends.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let BaselineDays = 60d;
let AgentMailboxes = dynamic([]);
let KnownRecipients = EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(BaselineDays) .. ago(LookbackDays))
    | where EmailDirection == "Outbound"
    | summarize by SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress;
let RecentOutbound = EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EmailDirection == "Outbound"
    | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
    | extend RecipientDomain = tolower(tostring(split(RecipientEmailAddress, "@")[1]))
    | where RecipientDomain !in~ ("gmail.com","outlook.com","hotmail.com")
    | project OutTime = Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, RecipientDomain, Subject, AttachmentCount;
let FirstTimeOutbound = RecentOutbound
    | join kind=leftanti KnownRecipients on SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress;
FirstTimeOutbound
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
    | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
    | project InboundTime = Timestamp, RecipientEmailAddress, InboundSubject = Subject, InboundSender = SenderFromAddress
  ) on $left.SenderFromAddress == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| where OutTime between (InboundTime .. InboundTime + 30m)
| extend DelayMin = datetime_diff('minute', OutTime, InboundTime)
| project InboundTime, OutTime, DelayMin, MailboxOwner = SenderFromAddress, ExternalRecipient = RecipientEmailAddress, RecipientDomain, InboundSender, InboundSubject, OutboundSubject = Subject, AttachmentCount
| order by OutTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let BaselineDays = 60d;
let KnownRecipients = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(BaselineDays) .. ago(LookbackDays))
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange" and Operation == "Send"
    | mv-expand Recipients
    | extend RecipientEmailAddress = tostring(Recipients)
    | summarize by SenderFromAddress = tostring(UserId), RecipientEmailAddress;
let RecentOutbound = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange" and Operation == "Send"
    | mv-expand Recipients
    | extend RecipientEmailAddress = tostring(Recipients)
    | extend RecipientDomain = tolower(tostring(split(RecipientEmailAddress, "@")[1]))
    | where RecipientDomain !in~ ("gmail.com","outlook.com","hotmail.com")
    | project OutTime = TimeGenerated, SenderFromAddress = tostring(UserId), RecipientEmailAddress, RecipientDomain, Subject = tostring(ItemName), ClientIPAddress;
let FirstTimeOutbound = RecentOutbound
    | join kind=leftanti KnownRecipients on SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress;
FirstTimeOutbound
| project OutTime, MailboxOwner = SenderFromAddress, ExternalRecipient = RecipientEmailAddress, RecipientDomain, Subject, ClientIPAddress
| order by OutTime desc
source:office365 @evt.name:(Send OR SendOnBehalf) @client.ip:* -@to_recipients.address:(*@yourdomain.com OR *@trusted-partner.com)

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstSeen from datamodel=Email.All_Email where All_Email.direction="outbound" by All_Email.src_user All_Email.recipient | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | rename src_user as sender, recipient as toAddr | eval recipDomain = mvindex(split(toAddr,"@"),1) | join type=inner sender [| tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as historicFirst from datamodel=Email.All_Email where All_Email.direction="outbound" by All_Email.src_user All_Email.recipient | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | rename src_user as sender, recipient as histRecip | where _time < relative_time(now(), "-30d") | stats values(histRecip) as knownRecipients by sender] | eval isFirstTime = if(isnull(mvfind(knownRecipients, toAddr)), 1, 0) | where isFirstTime=1 AND NOT recipDomain IN ("yourdomain.com","gmail.com","outlook.com") | table firstSeen sender toAddr recipDomain

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"

     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New GreatXML Exploit Bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 11 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse and MSNightmare) has released a new Windows BitLocker bypass dubbed GreatXML, a day after they published an exploit for Microsoft Defender. "This was an accidental discovery, it took a total of 4 hours to find this," the researcher said in a post on Blogger. "If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you're

CVEsCVE-2026-45585
ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1204.004 T1528

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Defender Offline Scan initiation - GreatXML vulnerability precondition · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Write of unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml to system recovery partition (GreatXML staging)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] reagentc.exe invocation enabling or remounting WinRE before reboot (GreatXML precondition) · [LLM] bcdedit recovery-sequence modification consistent with GreatXML WinRE pivot
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] BitLocker tamper attempt via manage-bde or BitLocker PowerShell after WinRE shell access · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Write of unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml to system recovery partition (GreatXML staging) AIWeaponization High
Detects the file-staging step of the GreatXML BitLocker bypass: writing unattend.xml and Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml to the root of the recovery partition prior to a Shift+Restart boot into WinRE. Recovery-partition XML writes from a logged-on user context are non-standard outside of Windows servicing and indicate the bypass precondition. Rationale: Article explicitly names the two files unattend.xml and Recovery/WindowsRE/ReAgent.xml dropped to the recovery partition root as the pre-reboot step of the bypass. Detecting either filename in a recovery-partition path is high-fidelity because legitimate writes there come from a tiny set of servicing binaries (TrustedInstaller, DISM, setup) which we exclude. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/windows-recovery-environment--windows-re--technical-reference • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/005/
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1112 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Feature-update (in-place upgrade) writing a new ReAgent.xml during servicing
  • MDT/SCCM task sequence dropping unattend.xml to a recovery image being built
  • OEM recovery image refresh utilities (Lenovo Vantage, HP Recovery Manager) regenerating WinRE
  • Sysprep generalize pass writing unattend.xml as part of imaging
  • Backup software snapshotting the recovery partition (rare since the partition is hidden)
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","DISM.exe","setup.exe","SetupHost.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","sysprep.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the writing process tree from DeviceProcessEvents on the same DeviceId in the 5 min before the file write — confirm it is not TrustedInstaller / DISM / a known imaging tool, and check whether the device just received a Windows feature update KB via Update table. Contain: isolate the host with Defender Live Response, disable Shift+Restart access by enforcing BitLocker pre-boot PIN, and pull the contents of the dropped XML for IR forensics before reboot. Hunt: pivot on the InitiatingProcessAccountName for any reagentc.exe /enable, MpCmdRun.exe -OfflineScan, or shutdown /r /o invocations in the previous 24h (the offline-scan precondition + WinRE entry sequence described by Chaotic Eclipse) across all endpoints.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("unattend.xml", "ReAgent.xml")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Recovery\", @"\WindowsRE\", @"\EFI\Microsoft\Recovery", @"\System Volume Information\Recovery")
| where not(InitiatingProcessAccountName endswith "$")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "DISM.exe", "setup.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("unattend.xml", "ReAgent.xml")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Recovery\", @"\WindowsRE\", @"\EFI\Microsoft\Recovery", @"\System Volume Information\Recovery")
| where not(ActorUsername endswith "$")
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "DISM.exe", "setup.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GreatXML BitLocker Bypass - Recovery Partition XML Staging
id: 9e6a5d52-2b4d-4f4b-9fa9-3f1d4c2a9a01
description: Detects writes of unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml into the Windows recovery partition / WinRE folder, the staging step of the GreatXML BitLocker bypass disclosed by Chaotic Eclipse in 2026-06.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1542.005
  - attack.t1112
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\unattend.xml'
      - '\ReAgent.xml'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Recovery\'
      - '\WindowsRE\'
      - '\EFI\Microsoft\Recovery\'
      - '\System Volume Information\Recovery'
  filter_servicing:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\DISM.exe'
      - '\setup.exe'
  condition: selection and selection_path and not filter_servicing
level: high
falsepositives:
  - Windows feature update / in-place upgrade writing a new ReAgent.xml during servicing
  - OEM recovery image refresh tools
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\unattend.xml OR *\Unattend.xml OR *\UNATTEND.XML OR *\ReAgent.xml OR *\reagent.xml OR *\REAGENT.XML)) (@TargetFilename:(*\Recovery\* OR *\recovery\* OR *\WindowsRE\* OR *\windowsre\* OR *\EFI\Microsoft\Recovery\*)) -@Image:(*\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\DISM.exe OR *\dism.exe OR *\setup.exe OR *\Setup.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\(unattend|ReAgent)\.xml$/i
| TargetFileName=/\\(Recovery|WindowsRE|EFI\\Microsoft\\Recovery|System Volume Information\\Recovery)\\/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|DISM|setup)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml" OR Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\WindowsRE\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\EFI\\Microsoft\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\System Volume Information\\Recovery\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml" OR Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\WindowsRE\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\EFI\\Microsoft\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\System Volume Information\\Recovery\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
reagentc.exe invocation enabling or remounting WinRE before reboot (GreatXML precondition) AIInstallation High
Detects reagentc.exe being run with flags that enable, remount, or stage WinRE — actions that are prerequisites for Chaotic Eclipse's GreatXML bypass to land. Legitimate reagentc.exe runs come almost exclusively from Windows servicing; user-context invocations are highly anomalous. Rationale: The Hacker News article notes the bypass requires booting into WinRE via Shift+Restart with the offline-scan/WinRE staged state. reagentc.exe is the canonical Windows utility for that staging; its /enable, /setreimage, /mountrec, and /boottore switches map directly to the steps the researcher describes (mounting the recovery folder and arming the next boot for WinRE). Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/reagentc-command-line-options • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT technician arming WinRE on a freshly-imaged device
  • Windows feature update repointing the recovery image during a KB install
  • BitLocker recovery troubleshooting performed by a help-desk admin
  • Lenovo/HP recovery refresh tooling calling reagentc /setreimage
  • Endpoint management agent (Intune ConfigMgr) running a baseline that re-enables WinRE
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","DISM.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","CcmExec.exe","IntuneManagementExtension.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: in DeviceProcessEvents, get the 10-minute parent process chain plus the issuing AccountName and confirm it is not a known IT service account / SCCM task sequence run. Contain: revoke interactive logon for the account on that device, force-disable WinRE (`reagentc /disable`) from a trusted admin context, and require BitLocker pre-boot PIN on the host. Hunt: pivot on the same DeviceId for matching unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml file writes to the recovery partition in the previous 1h and any subsequent shutdown /r /o or InitiateSystemShutdownEx call that would trigger a WinRE boot.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "reagentc.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/enable", "/setreimage", "/mountrec", "/boottore", "/setbootshelllink")
| where not(AccountName endswith "$")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "DISM.exe", "WindowsUpdateBox.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, IsInitiatingProcessRemoteSession
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\reagentc.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/enable", "/setreimage", "/mountrec", "/boottore", "/setbootshelllink")
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "DISM.exe", "WindowsUpdateBox.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: reagentc.exe Suspicious Invocation - GreatXML BitLocker Bypass Precondition
id: 7c9d1a44-aa11-4e72-bf65-3d8a4c5f7b22
description: Detects reagentc.exe being invoked with WinRE enable / remount / setreimage flags from non-servicing context, a precondition for the GreatXML BitLocker bypass.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1542.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\reagentc.exe'
  selection_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/enable'
      - '/setreimage'
      - '/mountrec'
      - '/boottore'
      - '/setbootshelllink'
  filter_servicing:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\DISM.exe'
      - '\WindowsUpdateBox.exe'
  condition: selection_img and selection_args and not filter_servicing
level: high
falsepositives:
  - Recovery image refresh by IT during host imaging
  - Windows feature update servicing
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\reagentc.exe OR *\ReAgentc.exe OR *\REAGENTC.EXE) @CommandLine:(*\/enable* OR *\/setreimage* OR *\/mountrec* OR *\/boottore*) -@ParentImage:(*\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\DISM.exe OR *\dism.exe OR *\WindowsUpdateBox.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\reagentc\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(\/enable|\/setreimage|\/mountrec|\/boottore|\/setbootshelllink)/i
| NOT (ParentBaseFileName=/^(TrustedInstaller|DISM|WindowsUpdateBox)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" (Processes.process="*/enable*" OR Processes.process="*/setreimage*" OR Processes.process="*/mountrec*" OR Processes.process="*/boottore*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" (Processes.process="*/enable*" OR Processes.process="*/setreimage*" OR Processes.process="*/mountrec*" OR Processes.process="*/boottore*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
BitLocker tamper attempt via manage-bde or BitLocker PowerShell after WinRE shell access AIActions on Objectives High
Detects post-bypass BitLocker tampering: manage-bde.exe disabling protectors or unlocking a volume, or PowerShell cmdlets Disable-BitLocker / Remove-BitLockerKeyProtector / Suspend-BitLocker. Chaotic Eclipse's GreatXML output is a shell with unrestricted BitLocker volume access; these are the natural follow-on actions. Rationale: The article's stated outcome is a shell with 'unrestricted access to the BitLocker volume.' Whatever the attacker does next on a real estate, manage-bde -off / -unlock / -protectors -disable and the equivalent BitLocker PowerShell module cmdlets are the only supported ways to act on that access — making this set a high-signal post-exploitation pivot. Cross-referenced to MITRE T1552.004. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/manage-bde • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/004/
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1486 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT decommissioning a laptop and suspending BitLocker prior to wipe
  • Firmware / TPM update KB requiring Suspend-BitLocker before reboot
  • Help-desk troubleshooting a wrong-PIN lockout with manage-bde -unlock
  • Endpoint-management baseline that rotates BitLocker key protectors
  • SCCM/Intune task sequence calling Suspend-BitLocker before an in-place upgrade
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("CcmExec.exe","IntuneManagementExtension.exe","MsSense.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "services.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the AccountName and parent chain — confirm it is not the SYSTEM-context Intune/SCCM agent and the host is not on the firmware-update wave. Contain: re-enable / resume BitLocker (`manage-bde -resume` or `Resume-BitLocker`), force a Tier 0 password reset for any AD accounts that were unlocked in the session, and rotate the recovery password in AAD/AD. Hunt: in the previous 24h on the same DeviceId look for reagentc.exe /enable, unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml writes to the recovery partition, and MpCmdRun.exe -OfflineScan (the offline-scan precondition the researcher calls out).
let bde_native = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "manage-bde.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-off", "-unlock", "-protectors", "-disable", "-forcerecovery");
let bde_ps = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Disable-BitLocker", "Remove-BitLockerKeyProtector", "Suspend-BitLocker", "Lock-BitLocker");
union bde_native, bde_ps
| where not(AccountName endswith "$")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, IsInitiatingProcessRemoteSession
| order by Timestamp desc
let bde_native = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\manage-bde.exe"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("-off", "-unlock", "-protectors", "-disable", "-forcerecovery");
let bde_ps = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe", "\\pwsh.exe")
    | where CommandLine has_any ("Disable-BitLocker", "Remove-BitLockerKeyProtector", "Suspend-BitLocker", "Lock-BitLocker");
union bde_native, bde_ps
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: BitLocker Protector Tamper - GreatXML Bypass Follow-on
id: 3a44e9d7-c512-44a1-9b1c-1c0e6f3a8c44
description: Detects manage-bde.exe or BitLocker PowerShell cmdlets disabling, unlocking, or removing key protectors, the natural follow-on after the GreatXML WinRE shell bypass.
references:

author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_bde:
    Image|endswith: '\manage-bde.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-off'
      - '-unlock'
      - '-protectors'

  - Pre-imaging steps that suspend BitLocker for an upcoming firmware update
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\manage-bde.exe OR *\Manage-bde.exe OR *\MANAGE-BDE.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*-off* OR *-unlock* OR *-protectors* OR *-disable* OR *-forcerecovery*)) OR (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*Disable-BitLocker* OR *Remove-BitLockerKeyProtector* OR *Suspend-BitLocker*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\manage-bde\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(-off|-unlock|-protectors|-disable|-forcerecovery)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(Disable-BitLocker|Remove-BitLockerKeyProtector|Suspend-BitLocker|Lock-BitLocker)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="manage-bde.exe" Processes.process IN ("*-off*","*-unlock*","*-protectors*","*-disable*","*-forcerecovery*")) OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*Disable-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Remove-BitLockerKeyProtector*" OR Processes.process="*Suspend-BitLocker*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="manage-bde.exe" Processes.process IN ("*-off*","*-unlock*","*-protectors*","*-disable*","*-forcerecovery*")) OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*Disable-BitLocker*" OR Processes.process="*Remove-BitLockerKeyProtector*" OR Processes.process="*Suspend-BitLocker*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Defender Offline Scan initiation - GreatXML vulnerability precondition AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects the Defender Offline Scan trigger that, per Chaotic Eclipse, is the precondition that puts a host in the vulnerable state for GreatXML. MpCmdRun.exe -Scan -ScheduleJob / offline-scan invocations and the OOBE registry trigger flag should be inventoried so the SOC can fingerprint which estate is exposed. Rationale: Chaotic Eclipse explicitly states: 'If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you're automatically vulnerable to a BitLocker bypass.' Inventorying MpCmdRun.exe offline-scan invocations gives the SOC the exposed-host list to scope patching and compensating controls (BitLocker pre-boot PIN). This is hunting tier — not a per-event alert. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/security/defender-endpoint/run-scan-microsoft-defender-antivirus • https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/defender/start-mpwdoscan
ATT&CKT1518.001 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • End user triggered Windows Security UI 'Microsoft Defender Offline scan' button
  • SOC-driven incident response running an offline scan on a suspected-compromised host
  • Help-desk troubleshooting a persistent malware infection
  • Vendor MDR agent invoking offline scan as part of a remediation playbook
  • Periodic compliance script forcing offline scan on a sample of endpoints
Response runbook
Triage: aggregate results into an exposure dashboard grouped by DeviceName and OS build — every device that has run offline scan is GreatXML-eligible until patched. Contain: push BitLocker pre-boot PIN policy via Intune/GPO to the affected devices and disable Shift+Restart access on the Windows lock screen via the `DisableLockScreenAppNotifications` / `ShutdownWithoutLogon` policies. Hunt: cross-reference the exposed-host list with subsequent reagentc.exe / unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml signals from the other GreatXML UCs in the same playbook.
let offlinescan_proc = DeviceProcessEvents

bcdedit recovery-sequence modification consistent with GreatXML WinRE pivot AIInstallation Medium
Detects bcdedit.exe modifying the boot configuration store to set a non-standard recovery sequence, mark recovery as enabled on the default entry, or copy a recovery boot entry — the BCD-side preparation an attacker would make to ensure the next reboot lands inside a controllable WinRE for the GreatXML chain. Rationale: Recovery partition tampering to land in a writable WinRE practically requires either reagentc.exe or bcdedit BCD-store changes that point /recoverysequence to a staged entry or flag /set {default} recoveryenabled Yes. The article does not name bcdedit directly but the GreatXML chain — drop XML, reboot into WinRE, get unrestricted BitLocker access — depends on this BCD plumbing being writable from the live OS. Sigma maps to MITRE T1542.001/005. Cross-checked against: • https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/drivers/devtest/bcdedit--set • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/001/
ATT&CKT1542.001 T1542.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT staff configuring dual-boot or PXE-recovery image on a workstation
  • Windows feature-update servicing repopulating the recovery BCD entry
  • Veeam / Macrium Reflect bootable-recovery agent installation
  • Vendor diagnostic tooling that adds a manufacturer recovery entry
  • Sysadmin running `bcdedit /enum` style commands which our filter already excludes (we only fire on state-changing verbs)
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","DISM.exe","WindowsUpdateBox.exe","setup.exe","SetupHost.exe","sysprep.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: capture the exact bcdedit command line, the resulting BCD entry, and the AccountName / parent chain — confirm not TrustedInstaller / DISM / SCCM imaging context. Contain: revert the BCD entry to its pre-change state (`bcdedit /deletevalue {default} recoverysequence` or restore from a known-good `bcdedit /export` backup), enforce Secure Boot + BitLocker pre-boot PIN. Hunt: same DeviceId for unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml writes to the recovery partition, reagentc.exe /enable or /setreimage, and any shutdown /r /o invocation within 30 minutes — the full GreatXML chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("recoverysequence", "recoveryenabled", "/copy", "/create", "/import", "bootsequence")
| where not(AccountName endswith "$")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "DISM.exe", "WindowsUpdateBox.exe", "setup.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, IsInitiatingProcessRemoteSession
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\bcdedit.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("recoverysequence", "recoveryenabled", "/copy", "/create", "/import", "bootsequence")
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "DISM.exe", "WindowsUpdateBox.exe", "setup.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Webserver process writes PHP-executable file to public web-root or upload directory (CVE-2026-48062) AIInstallation High
Detects php-fpm, nginx, httpd, w3wp, caddy or the php interpreter creating .php / .phar / .phtml / .phps / .pht files under common public web roots (public, webroot, htdocs, www, uploads, public_html). The CodeIgniter4 ext_in bypass advisory explicitly warns of this landing-on-disk artefact when applications save with the original client filename via $file->move($path). Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit conditions: 'save uploads using original client filename', 'store uploads in a web-accessible directory', 'allow PHP files to run from that directory'. The webserver-account UID writing a PHP-executable extension under /public is precisely the post-validation-bypass artefact. Filename-extension list (.php/.phar/.phtml/.phps/.pht) covers all PHP-handler-mapped extensions and matches the article's exact bypass example (shell.php).
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003 T1036.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Composer install / git pull during a legitimate deploy, when the webserver UID writes vendored .php files into public/
  • CMS plugin or theme installer writing .php under public/uploads/ via an in-app admin upload (WordPress, Drupal extension store)
  • Dev environment with hot-reload writing into the document root under the webserver UID
  • CodeIgniter4 cache writers writing PHP cache shards to writable/cache (filter via the writable/ prefix)
  • Imagick or thumbnailer wrappers that legitimately move processed assets into /public/uploads/thumbs/ — if any are .php-suffixed (rare)
Suppression filter
and not (FolderPath has_any (@"\writable\","/writable/",@"\vendor\","/vendor/",@"\.git\","/.git/")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer","git pull","git checkout","git clone","deploy")) and not (FileName startswith "index.php")
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the file at FolderPath\FileName from a forensic copy — confirm presence of webshell strings (eval, system, base64_decode, assert, passthru) or polyglot GIF/JFIF magic followed by `<?php`. Pull the SHA256 to VirusTotal / internal sandbox. Identify the upload endpoint by tracing InitiatingProcessId backwards through DeviceProcessEvents. 2) Contain: quarantine the file (rename to .quarantine, chmod 000), block the source IP at WAF, and disable the affected CodeIgniter4 application or stop the webserver if active exploitation is ongoing. 3) Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessId for outbound NetworkConnect/DnsRequest from php-fpm/w3wp in the next 24h, look for additional .php drops on neighbour hosts behind the same load balancer, and confirm CodeIgniter4 version inventory against CVE-2026-48062 (UC 4 below).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","caddy.exe","php.exe")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phps" or FileName endswith ".pht"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\public\", @"\webroot\", @"\htdocs\", @"\www\", @"\uploads\", @"\public_html\", "/public/", "/webroot/", "/htdocs/", "/www/", "/uploads/", "/public_html/")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated" or EventType =~ "FileRenamed" or EventType =~ "FileModified"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","httpd","nginx","w3wp","caddy","php.exe","php")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phar","phtml","phps","pht")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\public\",@"\webroot\",@"\htdocs\",@"\www\",@"\uploads\",@"\public_html\","/public/","/webroot/","/htdocs/","/www/","/uploads/","/public_html/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Webserver / PHP interpreter writes PHP-executable file to public web root (CVE-2026-48062)
id: 2c54e1a8-3b4e-4d8c-9a9a-3f7b2a1c4d6e
description: |
  Detects webserver / interpreter processes (php-fpm, php-cgi, nginx, httpd, w3wp, caddy, php) writing
  PHP-executable files (.php/.phar/.phtml/.phps/.pht) under common public web-roots. This is the
  landing-on-disk artefact of the CodeIgniter4 ext_in upload-validation bypass (CVE-2026-48062) where
  a file named shell.php with GIF-like content passed `ext_in[avatar,gif]`.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1036.008
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\php-fpm.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\caddy.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.phar'
      - '.phtml'
      - '.phps'
      - '.pht'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\public\'
      - '\webroot\'
      - '\htdocs\'
      - '\www\'
      - '\uploads\'
      - '\public_html\'
  condition: selection_process and selection_ext and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate composer install / git pull writing new PHP modules under public during deploy
  - CMS plugin or theme installer dropping PHP includes in public web-root
  - Developer hot-reload pushing PHP into the public dir on a non-prod host
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\php-fpm.exe OR *\\PHP-FPM.exe OR *\\php-cgi.exe OR *\\httpd.exe OR *\\HTTPD.exe OR *\\nginx.exe OR *\\Nginx.exe OR *\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.exe OR *\\caddy.exe OR *\\php.exe OR *\\PHP.exe) @TargetFilename:(*.php OR *.phar OR *.phtml OR *.phps OR *.pht) (@TargetFilename:(*\\public\\* OR *\\webroot\\* OR *\\htdocs\\* OR *\\www\\* OR *\\uploads\\* OR *\\public_html\\*) OR @TargetFilename:(*/public/* OR */webroot/* OR */htdocs/* OR */www/* OR */uploads/* OR */public_html/*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|httpd|nginx|w3wp|caddy|php)\.exe$/i
| TargetFileName=/\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|pht)$/i
| regex("(\\\\|/)(public|webroot|htdocs|www|uploads|public_html)(\\\\|/)", field=TargetFileName, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count(as=writes))
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Filesystem.file_hash) as sha256 values(Filesystem.process) as process_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","renamed") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","caddy.exe","php.exe") AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phps" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.pht") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\public\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\webroot\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\htdocs\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\www\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\public_html\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/public/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/webroot/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/htdocs/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/www/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/uploads/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/public_html/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - last_seen
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Filesystem.file_hash) as sha256 values(Filesystem.process) as process_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","renamed") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","caddy.exe","php.exe") AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phps" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.pht") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\public\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\webroot\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\htdocs\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\www\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\public_html\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/public/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/webroot/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/htdocs/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/www/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/uploads/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/public_html/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - last_seen
Webserver / PHP interpreter spawns shell or LOLBin — post-upload RCE indicator AIExploitation High
Detects php-fpm, php-cgi, nginx, httpd, w3wp, caddy or php.exe directly spawning cmd/powershell/sh/bash or LOLBins (whoami, net, certutil, curl, wget, bitsadmin). The CodeIgniter4 ext_in bypass culminates in arbitrary code execution when the dropped PHP file is requested — this catches the resulting child process even when the on-disk artefact is missed. Rationale: Article's stated impact is 'arbitrary code execution' via the dropped PHP file being requested by the attacker. The PHP interpreter forking a shell or recon LOLBin is the classic post-webshell-execution shape and is extremely uncommon in production PHP stacks outside of imagemagick/ffmpeg wrappers, which can be excluded via cmdline. Parent-child pair is the high-fidelity signal — neither side alone qualifies.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PHP applications using exec/system to call ImageMagick (convert), ffmpeg, or wkhtmltopdf — flag and allowlist by cmdline
  • WordPress / Drupal cron jobs shelling out to wp-cli or drush from php-fpm
  • Application-installed monitoring agents using whoami/hostname from PHP for diagnostics
  • Composer post-install / post-update scripts running during deploys
  • PHP-based queue workers (php-resque, Laravel Horizon) that legitimately spawn child processes for job isolation
Suppression filter
and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("convert","ffmpeg","wkhtmltopdf","gs ","ghostscript","imagemagick","wp-cli","drush","artisan","composer")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer install","composer update","post-install","post-update"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full ProcessCommandLine and InitiatingProcessCommandLine — webshells frequently pass attacker input as the arg (e.g. 'cmd.exe /c whoami'). Pull the upstream PHP request from W3CIISLog/access logs around Timestamp ±5s using ProcessId correlation. 2) Contain: kill the PHP-FPM worker pool (systemctl restart php-fpm or iisreset), block source IP, and pull the on-disk PHP files written by that worker UID in the last 24h for analysis. 3) Hunt: enumerate further child processes from any php-fpm/w3wp in the org over the last 7d (DeviceProcessEvents | parent in PHP set), check for outbound C2 from those workers (DeviceNetworkEvents), and run UC1 to find the webshell artefact.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","caddy.exe","php.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","reg.exe","hostname.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\php-fpm.exe","\\php-cgi.exe","\\httpd.exe","\\nginx.exe","\\w3wp.exe","\\caddy.exe","\\php.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\whoami.exe","\\net.exe","\\net1.exe","\\reg.exe","\\hostname.exe","\\ipconfig.exe","\\systeminfo.exe","\\tasklist.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ProcessId, NewProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HTTP multipart upload: image Content-Type with PHP/executable filename extension (CVE-2026-48062 exploit shape) AIDelivery High
Detects the exact bypass condition described in the advisory at the request layer: a multipart upload where the Content-Type header indicates an image (image/gif, image/png, image/jpeg) but the multipart filename ends in .php / .phtml / .phar / .phps. CodeIgniter4's pre-4.7.3 ext_in rule trusts the MIME-guessed extension and accepts the file. Requires WAF or application-level HTTP body parsing — IIS / Apache access logs alone do not expose multipart filenames. Rationale: Article names the exact rule: `ext_in[avatar,gif]` is bypassed by `shell.php` containing GIF-like content. The detectable signature at ingress is the multipart-part mismatch: declared Content-Type=image/* AND filename=*.php. WAF / app-tier HTTP logging is required (IIS/Apache plain access logs don't expose multipart filenames), so falcon_logscale_query and defender_kql are intentionally empty — FDR and Defender DeviceNetworkEvents don't carry decoded multipart part headers.
ATT&CKT1190 T1036.008
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal pentest / red-team running automated file-upload bypass tests against the same endpoint
  • Bug-bounty researcher submitting test payloads via a known WAF-allowed source IP
  • Misconfigured client uploading a .php file that the client incorrectly tagged as image/jpeg (rare, usually a browser-side bug)
  • WAF replay/debug traffic from QA environment that has been mirrored into the prod log stream
Suppression filter
and not (SourceIP in ("<pentest-egress-ip>","<bug-bounty-egress-ip>")) and not (UA has_any ("Burp","sqlmap","OWASP ZAP") and SourceIP startswith "10.")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full multipart body from the WAF and confirm whether the file was accepted by the upload endpoint (HTTP 200/302 vs 4xx). Identify the target CodeIgniter4 host(s) and the resolved file path on disk by tracing the SrcIpAddr to backend logs. 2) Contain: block SourceIP at the WAF, drop any uploaded artefact from disk after preserving a forensic copy, and verify CodeIgniter4 framework version >= 4.7.3 on the receiving app. 3) Hunt: search the prior 30d of WAF logs for the same SrcIpAddr against any upload endpoint org-wide, and pivot to UC1 / UC2 to see whether the dropped file was executed.
let UploadEndpoints = dynamic(["/upload","/avatar","/uploads","/file","/profile","/image","/photo","/picture"]);
let ImageMimes = dynamic(["image/gif","image/jpeg","image/jpg","image/png","image/webp","image/bmp","gif","jpeg","png","jpg","webp","bmp"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
    | where RequestURL has_any (UploadEndpoints)
    | where FileType in~ (ImageMimes)
    | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|pht)$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=DeviceVendor, SourceIP, DestHost=DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, FileName, FileType, UA=RequestClientApplication
),
(
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Url has_any (UploadEndpoints)
    | where FileMimeType in~ (ImageMimes)
    | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|pht)$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=EventVendor, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestHost=HttpHostName, RequestURL=Url, RequestMethod=HttpMethod, FileName, FileType=FileMimeType, UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HTTP multipart upload — image MIME with PHP/executable filename extension (CVE-2026-48062)
id: 9f4e8b7c-2d6a-4c5e-8d1b-7a3c9e2f5d1a
description: |
  Multipart-form upload whose part declares an image MIME type (image/gif|png|jpeg|webp|bmp) but whose
  filename ends in a PHP-executable extension (.php/.phar/.phtml/.phps/.pht). This is the precise bypass
  condition for CodeIgniter4 CVE-2026-48062 where the ext_in rule trusts the MIME-guessed extension.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1036.008
logsource:
  category: webserver
  product: waf
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: POST
  selection_mime:
    file-mime:
      - 'image/gif'
      - 'image/jpeg'
      - 'image/png'
      - 'image/webp'
      - 'image/bmp'
  selection_ext:
    filename|re|i: '\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|pht)$'
  condition: selection_method and selection_mime and selection_ext
falsepositives:
  - Security researcher / pentester running automated upload-validation tests against the same endpoint
  - Misconfigured CMS theme installer briefly carrying both image MIME and php filename for a polyglot widget
level: high
(source:apache.access OR source:nginx.access OR source:iis OR source:cloudflare OR source:imperva OR source:f5) @http.method:POST (@http.url_details.path:*upload* OR @http.url_details.path:*avatar* OR @http.url_details.path:*uploads* OR @http.url_details.path:*file* OR @http.url_details.path:*profile* OR @http.url_details.path:*image*) (@http.request.body.content_type:image\/* OR @http.headers.content_type:multipart\/form-data*) (@http.upload.filename:(*.php OR *.phar OR *.phtml OR *.phps OR *.pht OR *.PHP OR *.PHAR OR *.PHTML))

`waf` OR `cef` request_method=POST (uri_path="*/upload*" OR uri_path="*/avatar*" OR uri_path="*/uploads*" OR uri_path="*/file*" OR uri_path="*/profile*" OR uri_path="*/image*") (file_mime="image/gif" OR file_mime="image/jpeg" OR file_mime="image/png" OR file_mime="image/webp" OR file_mime="image/bmp" OR content_type="image/*")

Vulnerable CodeIgniter4 framework inventory (CVE-2026-48062, < 4.7.3) AIReconnaissance High
Asset-state hunt: enumerates hosts where Defender TVM or Sentinel inventory reports composer:codeigniter4/framework at a version < 4.7.3, scoped by the CVE-2026-48062 advisory. Use this to drive patch deployment and prioritise application-layer monitoring for the run-time detections in UC1-UC3. Rationale: Pure inventory pivot using the CVE explicitly named in the advisory (CVE-2026-48062) and the affected package `composer:codeigniter4/framework` < 4.7.2. Sigma omitted because asset-state inventory is not a single-event-shape detection. Datadog/Falcon/CloudWatch omitted because composer-level framework inventory is not in their standard schemas — Defender TVM and Sentinel TVM are the canonical surfaces.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Hosts with CodeIgniter4 vendored under a non-production path (CI runner image, archived backup) which is not actively served
  • Container hosts whose TVM scan reports the package inside a stopped image layer rather than a running container
  • Dev-only laptops with cloned codeigniter4/CodeIgniter4 git source for contributor work
  • Vendored CodeIgniter4 inside a parent application that ships its own patched fork (rare — verify with the app team)
Response runbook
1) Triage: cross-reference each DeviceName with the CMDB to identify owning team, application name, and exposure (internet-facing vs internal). Prioritise IsInternetFacing=true. 2) Contain: open a change ticket to upgrade composer:codeigniter4/framework to >= 4.7.3, and for any host that cannot patch within 72h apply the advisory's listed workarounds (move uploads outside webroot, use $file->store() or $file->move($path, $file->getRandomName()), disable PHP execution in upload dirs). 3) Hunt: enable UC1/UC2/UC3 alerting on the affected hosts and review the prior 30d of WAF logs against any upload endpoints those apps expose.

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48062")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48062")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
